target.title: feat(hooks): add waitForResult mode to POST /hooks/agent endpoint
target.body:
## Summary

Implements the `waitForResult` mode for `POST /hooks/agent` as proposed in #49019.

When a caller sends `{"message": "...", "waitForResult": true}`, the endpoint holds the connection open until the agent turn completes and returns a machine-readable result — no polling or `sessions_history` stitching required.

Also adds `announceToMain: false` to suppress the post-run summary event for fully machine-driven flows.

## Changes

- **`src/gateway/hooks.ts`**
  - Rename `blocking` → `waitForResult` (aligns with #49019 naming)
  - Add `announceToMain?: boolean` field (default `true`; `false` suppresses main-session summary event)
  - Parse both fields in `normalizeAgentPayload`

- **`src/gateway/server/hooks.ts`**
  - `dispatchAgentHook` returns `Promise<{ runId, sessionKey, outputText?, agentError? }>`
  - `announceToMain: false` gates the `shouldAnnounceHookRunResult` path

- **`src/gateway/server/hooks-request-handler.ts`**
  - Response shape aligned with #49019:
    - `status: "completed" | "accepted" | "error"`
    - `sessionKey` (resolved session for the run)
    - `result` (agent output text, present only when `waitForResult: true`)

- **`extensions/slack/package.json`** *(drive-by fix, last commit on this branch)*
  - Declare `typebox` as a runtime dependency. `extensions/slack/src/message-tool-api.ts` imports `typebox` (added in 98543edd3d) but the package never declared it, so the `extension-runtime-dependencies` contract test fails on every PR rebased onto current `main`. This unblocks our CI and any other PR hitting the same wall. Happy to spin it out into a separate PR if you'd prefer.

## Request / response example

```json
// Request
{
  "message": "Run this protocol task",
  "agentId": "bridge-protocol",
  "sessionKey": "hook:bridge:run-123",
  "deliver": false,
  "waitForResult": true,
  "announceToMain": false,
  "timeoutSeconds": 30
}

// Response
{
  "ok": true,
  "status": "completed",
  "runId": "<uuid>",
  "sessionKey": "agent:bridge-protocol:hook:bridge:run-123",
  "result": "<agent output text>"
}
```

## Backwards compatibility

- `waitForResult` omitted (or `false`) → identical async behavior as before, response gains `status: "accepted"` and `sessionKey`
- `announceToMain` omitted → defaults `true`, no change in observable behavior

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed:** `POST /hooks/agent` previously returned only `{ runId }` and the agent ran asynchronously. Callers who needed the agent's output had to poll `sessions_history` and stitch the result themselves. This change adds `waitForResult: true` so the endpoint blocks until the isolated agent turn finishes and returns `{ status, runId, sessionKey, result }`, plus `announceToMain: false` to suppress the post-run summary event for fully machine-driven flows.

**Real environment tested:** OpenClaw built from this PR's branch (HEAD `3d765d0a5c`), packed with `pnpm pack` into `openclaw-2026.5.10-beta.1.tgz`, installed into a real OpenClaw container (Tide `corp` instance, host `tide-host-01`, Linux + Docker, port `127.0.0.1:19020 → 18789`). The container's prior build was backed up to `/opt/openclaw.bak`, the new build was placed at `/opt/openclaw`, the container was restarted, and `/health` returned `{"ok":true,"status":"live"}` before the proof requests. After the proof was captured the instance was rolled back to its prior build and confirmed healthy again.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Build the rebased PR, install it into a real OpenClaw container, exercise both code paths, capture logs, and roll back. Concrete commands (bash):

```bash
cd ~/work/openclaw-pr-67433 && pnpm pack    
scp openclaw-2026.5.10-beta.1.tgz tide-host-01:/tmp/
ssh tide-host-01 'docker cp /tmp/openclaw-2026.5.10-beta.1.tgz tide-corp:/tmp/ && \
  docker exec tide-corp sh -c "cd /tmp && tar xzf openclaw-2026.5.10-beta.1.tgz && \
    mv /opt/openclaw /opt/openclaw.bak && mv /tmp/package /opt/openclaw" && \
  docker restart tide-corp'
curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:19020/hooks/agent \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <hook-token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"message":"Reply with exactly the string PROOF-OK and nothing else.",
       "name":"PR67433-proof","agentId":"main",
       "waitForResult":true,"announceToMain":false,
       "deliver":false,"timeoutSeconds":60}'
curl -sS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:19020/hooks/agent \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <hook-token>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"message":"hello","name":"PR67433-proof-async",
       "agentId":"main","deliver":false}'
docker logs tide-corp --since 30m 2>&1 | grep -i hook
ssh tide-host-01 'docker exec tide-corp sh -c "rm -rf /opt/openclaw && \
  mv /opt/openclaw.bak /opt/openclaw" && docker restart tide-corp'
```

(Steps map 1:1 to the commands above: pack → scp → install in container & restart → Test 1 (`waitForResult: true`) → Test 2 (legacy async) → capture logs → roll back.)

**Evidence after fix:**

target.title: feat(googlechat): support Application Default Credentials for outbound auth
target.body:
## Summary

- **Problem:** the Google Chat channel only authenticates outbound calls with an explicit service-account credential (`serviceAccount` / `serviceAccountRef` / `serviceAccountFile`). There is no Application Default Credentials path, so a GCP-hosted gateway must keep a long-lived downloaded SA key on disk even though the runtime already has a usable identity (GCE metadata server / workload identity).
- **Change:** add an opt-in `channels.googlechat.serviceAccountAdc: true`. When set and no explicit credential is configured, credential resolution returns a new `"adc"` source; the channel activates normally and the auth runtime constructs `GoogleAuth` without a key, falling back to the ambient ADC chain using the `chat.bot` scope.
- **Outcome:** GCP deployments can run Google Chat keyless — the attached service account / workload identity signs outbound requests, with no SA key in config or on disk. This mirrors how the Vertex model path already uses ADC.
- **Out of scope / unchanged:** the flag is opt-in and defaults off — existing `serviceAccount*` behavior is untouched, and an explicit credential always takes precedence. Inbound webhook auth (already keyless via `audience`/JWT) is not changed.
- **Reviewers, please focus on:** the new `"adc"` value in `accounts.ts` (`resolveCredentialsFromConfig`) and that it threads through the existing `credentialSource !== "none"` gates so the channel activates; the auth runtime already builds `GoogleAuth` with no credentials when none resolve, so no change was needed there.

## Linked context

Closes # _(none)_

Related # _(none found — searched issues for ADC/keyless Google Chat)_

Was this requested by a maintainer or owner? No — contributor-initiated. We run OpenClaw on GCP and want to eliminate Google Chat service-account key files.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Google Chat outbound auth required a downloaded SA key; with this patch it authenticates keyless via ADC.
- **Real environment tested:** OpenClaw `v2026.6.6` + this patch, built into the Docker image and deployed on a GCE VM (arm64). Google Chat app configured (Workspace add-on, app-url audience). The VM's attached service account is the Chat app's posting identity and carries the `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/chat.bot` access scope. No service-account key exists in the config or on the VM disk.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** set `channels.googlechat.serviceAccountAdc: true` with **no** `serviceAccountRef`/`serviceAccountFile` (and removed the on-disk key those previously pointed at), restarted the gateway, then sent the bot a direct message and confirmed the reply.
- **Evidence after fix:** Copied live output / redacted runtime logs and a reply screenshot from a real GCE deployment (identifiers — space id, message/run/session ids, add-on principal, webhook path key — redacted). Three artifacts:

  **(1) Keyless config in effect** — the live `channels.googlechat` block: ADC on, no credential of any kind configured:
  ```json
  "googlechat": {
    "serviceAccountAdc": true,
    "audienceType": "app-url",
    "audience": "https://<redacted-host>/<redacted-path-key>/googlechat",
    "webhookPath": "/<redacted-path-key>/googlechat"
  }
  ```

  **(2) Runtime round-trip log** — an inbound DM driven all the way to a delivered reply on `channel=googlechat`, with no credential/key anywhere in the pipeline (note the only outbound HTTP the transport logs is the model call to Anthropic; the Chat send is the dispatch that completes at the end):
  ```
  [diagnostic] message received: channel=googlechat chatId=googlechat:spaces/<redacted> messageId=<redacted> sessionKey=agent:main:main source=dispatchInboundMessage
  [agent/embedded] embedded run start: runId=<redacted> provider=anthropic model=claude-opus-4-7 messageChannel=googlechat
  [provider-transport-fetch] [model-fetch] response provider=anthropic api=anthropic-messages model=claude-opus-4-7 status=200
  [googlechat] embedded run agent end: runId=<redacted> isError=false
  [diagnostic] message dispatch completed: channel=googlechat sessionKey=agent:main:main source=replyResolver outcome=completed duration=5675ms
  [diagnostic] message processed: channel=googlechat chatId=googlechat:spaces/<redacted> outcome=completed duration=5758ms
  ```

  **(3) Reply artifact** — the bot's reply rendered in Google Chat (keyless; no SA key configured):

  ![Keyless Google Chat reply — the bot ("Cora") replies to a DM with serviceAccountAdc enabled and no service-account key configured](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bc604362-c55e-41bc-8bee-a169d01b1cf1)

  For completeness, the gateway boot with `serviceAccountAdc: true` and no Chat credential — the channel loads and mounts its webhook with no credential error:
  ```
  [googlechat] [default] starting Google Chat webhook
  [gateway] ready
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** the googlechat channel activates on `credentialSource: "adc"` and mounts its webhook; an inbound DM is processed to `outcome=completed` and the bot replies (screenshot). Because **no credential of any kind is configured and no key file is on disk**, the outbound post to `chat.googleapis.com` can only have authenticated via the ambient ADC identity — the VM's attached service account (`chat.bot` scope) through the GCE metadata server. A misconfigured/absent ADC identity would fail the outbound send; the delivered reply confirms the ADC path worked.
- **What was not tested:** the `project-number` audience type (we use `app-url`); non-GCE ADC sources such as `GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS` (only the GCE metadata path was exercised); multi-account `channels.googlechat.accounts.*` setups (see review note below).
- **Proof limitations or environment constraints:** private deployment; identifiers redacted. I did not capture a discrete metadata-server token-fetch log line: the ADC access token is cached in-process after first acquisition, so a subsequent DM within the token lifetime triggers no fresh metadata call to log. The token-source claim therefore rests on (a) no credential being configured anywhere and (b) the outbound reply succeeding — which together are only possible via the ambient ADC identity.
- **Before evidence (optional):** before the patch, the same config failed at startup — `channels.googlechat: invalid config: must not have additional properties: "serviceAccountAdc"` (unknown key), and with no credential at all the channel stayed `credentialSource: "none"` and never mounted its webhook.

## Tests and validation

Commands run (rebased onto current `main`, regenerated artifacts, re-run):
- `pnpm test:extension googlechat` — **pass**, including the added `resolveGoogleChatAccount` cases (`serviceAccountAdc` → `source: "adc"`; explicit credential still wins) and the schema-accept case.
- `pnpm config:channels:check`, `pnpm config:docs:check`, `pnpm config:schema:check` — green after regenerating `bundled-channel-config-metadata.generated.ts` and the config-doc baseline (`config:channels:gen` / `config:docs:gen`).

Regression coverage added: `extensions/googlechat/src/setup.test.ts` (resolver: adc source + explicit-wins) and `extensions/googlechat/src/config-schema.test.ts` (schema accepts `serviceAccountAdc`).

What failed before this fix: unknown-key config rejection, and a credential-less channel never activating (`credentialSource: "none"`).

## Risk checklist

- User-visible behavior change? **No** — opt-in, default off.
- Config/env/migration change? **Yes** — new optional config key `channels.googlechat.serviceAccountAdc`.
- Security/auth/secrets/network/tool-exec change? **Yes** — adds an ADC auth path for Chat outbound and removes the need to store a service-account key file.
- Highest-risk area: an operator enabling `serviceAccountAdc` where ADC is unavailable/unauthorized would see outbound auth fail at runtime.
- Mitigation: strictly opt-in; an explicit credential always takes precedence; the channel only uses ADC when the operator asks for it and supplies no key. Docs note the required `chat.bot` scope.

## Current review state

- Next action: maintainer review + CI authorization (heavy CI lanes are gated behind first-time-contributor workflow-actor approval).
- Rebased onto current `main`; generated artifacts (`bundled-channel-config-metadata`, config-doc baseline) regenerated; real-behavior proof above (round-trip runtime log + reply screenshot).
- **Addressed since the ClawSweeper review — multi-account credential surfaces:** `serviceAccountAdc` is now treated as credential-owned config everywhere the older key fields are — registered as an implicit-default-account key, excluded from `accounts.default` shared defaults (no cross-account ambient-ADC inheritance), and cleared alongside the key fields on default-account deletion. Added multi-account regression tests in `extensions/googlechat/src/accounts.test.ts`.
- **Open for maintainer direction — Compute metadata-server boundary:** ADC resolves tokens via `google-auth-library`/`gcp-metadata`'s standard metadata path, outside any Chat-specific fetch guard. This is opt-in (`serviceAccountAdc` defaults off) and our own deployment is single-account on GCE, so ADC-via-metadata is the intended path for us — flagging for an explicit accept-or-guard decision, and happy to add a guard instead if preferred.

target.title: fix: require exact markdown frontmatter delimiters
target.body:
Closes #101769

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users writing Markdown command, hook, skill, workshop proposal, or metadata files could have content that starts with non-delimiter text like `---not` or `----` interpreted as YAML frontmatter.

That could make OpenClaw read unexpected metadata and strip or alter body text even though the Markdown did not begin with a whole `---` delimiter line.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared markdown-core frontmatter parser now requires exact `---` delimiter lines for both opening and closing fences. Bundled Claude command body extraction and skill workshop proposal stripping now reuse the same shared delimiter extractor instead of keeping separate prefix-based logic.

This keeps metadata parsing and body stripping aligned without adding config, compatibility shims, or plugin-specific policy.

## User Impact

Markdown files can now safely begin with dash-prefixed text that is not a frontmatter delimiter. Valid `---` frontmatter blocks still parse normally, while `---not` and `----` remain part of the Markdown body.

## Evidence

Before the fix, the reported source-level case parsed unexpected metadata:

```text
node --import tsx --input-type=module - <<'EOF'
import { parseFrontmatterBlock } from './packages/markdown-core/src/frontmatter.ts';
const content = '---not\nname: nope\n---not\nbody';
console.log(JSON.stringify(parseFrontmatterBlock(content)));
EOF
{"name":"nope"}
```

After the fix, the final source-level proof keeps invalid delimiter text as Markdown and still accepts a valid block:

```text
node --import tsx --input-type=module - <<'EOF'
import { parseFrontmatterBlock, stripFrontmatterBlock } from './packages/markdown-core/src/frontmatter.ts';
const invalid = '---not\nname: nope\n---not\nbody';
const valid = '---\nname: valid\n---\nbody';
console.log('invalid', JSON.stringify(parseFrontmatterBlock(invalid)), JSON.stringify(stripFrontmatterBlock(invalid)));
console.log('valid', JSON.stringify(parseFrontmatterBlock(valid)), JSON.stringify(stripFrontmatterBlock(valid)));
EOF
invalid {} "---not\nname: nope\n---not\nbody"
valid {"name":"valid"} "body"
```

target.title: feat(computer-use): control macOS nodes via screenshots and input injection
target.body:
Related: #97333
Related: #97938
Related: #69799
Related: #44759

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw could screenshot a paired macOS node but could not act on it: there was no way for an agent to move the pointer, click, type, scroll, or press keys on a node. Computer-use ("drive the desktop from a screenshot loop") was a repeatedly requested capability (#97333) with no end-to-end path — no input-injection node command, no agent tool, and no permission/arming model to make it safe.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds the first end-to-end computer-use path, scoped to macOS nodes, as a bundled `computer-use` plugin plus a native node executor.

- **Node protocol** (`openclaw.node.computer.v1`): a low-risk `computer.status` read (display geometry, cursor, permission state) and a dangerous `computer.input` write (one action: move / click / mouse down·up / drag / scroll / key / type / hold). Screenshots reuse the existing `screen.snapshot`.
- **macOS executor**: the Mac app node handles `computer.*` natively via CoreGraphics event injection, gated behind a new "Allow Computer Control" setting (default off) and Accessibility trust. Pointer coordinates are interpreted in reference-screenshot pixels and mapped back to global screen points, so the model can click where it sees.
- **Plugin**: registers the `computer` agent tool (drives the screenshot→act loop, one action per call, returning a fresh screenshot to the model), and two node-invoke policies. `computer.input` is `dangerous` — it requires operator opt-in via `gateway.nodes.allowCommands` plus per-session approval, with `allow-always` arming the node for a bounded window (`computer arm/disarm/status`).
- **Safety**: screenshots go to the model, not auto-delivered to chat channels (avoids the on-screen-secret leak class in #44759); the executor lives in the app that holds the TCC grants, not an ambient CLI binary (the concern in #69799); screen content is treated as untrusted input (prompt-injection posture documented in the skill and tool description).

Non-goals (follow-ups): provider-native Anthropic `computer_20251124` tool-type transport, Linux/Windows/sandbox-desktop executors, and time-bounded persistent arming beyond the in-window model.

## User Impact

On a paired macOS node with the plugin enabled, "Allow Computer Control" turned on, and `computer.input` opted into `gateway.nodes.allowCommands`, an agent can look at the screen and operate the Mac — click buttons, type into fields, use keyboard shortcuts, scroll, and drag — with an explicit approval/arming gate. It is macOS-only for now and off by default at every layer.

## Evidence

- **Swift (validated locally):** `apps/shared/OpenClawKit` builds clean; the OpenClaw app target compiles (`swift build --target OpenClaw`, 1070/1070). Swift tests pass: `swift test` → 44 tests across `ComputerInputGeometryTests` (coordinate mapping + Codable, 7/7), `ComputerKeyMapTests` (key-name/chord mapping), and `MacNodeModeCoordinatorTests`/`MacNodeRuntimeTests` (caps/command advertisement + dispatch). `swiftformat --lint` clean.
- **TypeScript:** `pnpm test extensions/computer-use` → 29 passed (4 files). Covers the arming gate (`input-policy.test.ts`: not-armed → approval; deny/null → not invoked; allow-once → invoke without arming; allow-always → armed with expiry; already-armed → invoked without approval; non-macOS → rejected), the tool schema + convenience-click translation, arm-state expiry, and plugin registration (two policies + tool + command + keyed store). Package-manifest contract test → 40 passed. `oxfmt --check` clean. Plugin inventory regenerated (`pnpm plugins:inventory:gen`).
- **Live input injection** (CGEvent + Accessibility TCC) requires a real Mac with the app built and Accessibility granted; it is **not** exercised by CI. This is the remaining manual verification gate before land.

Stacked on the Computer Use manifest contract PR (base). Do not land before live-injection verification on a real Mac.

target.title: fix(browser): keep Playwright truncation UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## Summary

- Keep Playwright browser response-body truncation UTF-16 safe.
- Keep Playwright AI snapshot truncation UTF-16 safe before appending the page-too-large marker.
- Keep Chrome MCP AI snapshot truncation UTF-16 safe for the same `maxChars` route contract.
- Add regression coverage for all three truncation paths.

## What Problem This Solves

Browser tool output can be truncated at a raw JavaScript string index. When the limit lands between the two code units of an emoji or other surrogate pair, OpenClaw can return a dangling surrogate in the browser response body or AI snapshot text.

## User Impact

Users inspecting browser response bodies or page snapshots can see malformed Unicode output when content is truncated near an emoji boundary. The fix preserves the existing size limits and truncation markers while avoiding invalid UTF-16 in returned browser tool text.

- **Why it matters / User impact:** Browser response body and AI snapshot output are directly shown to the agent/user; malformed UTF-16 can make truncated browser evidence confusing or lossy when page text or response bodies contain emoji.
- **What did NOT change:** Only the Playwright response-body truncation boundary and the two browser AI snapshot truncation boundaries changed. Routing, navigation, network matching, byte limits, provider behavior, channel behavior, config, and unrelated browser tool paths are unchanged and out of scope.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** The source-of-truth contract is that browser helper output must remain bounded and valid UTF-16. The canonical helper for that contract is `truncateUtf16Safe` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime`, which the browser extension already imports, so this patch stays inside the existing plugin architecture boundary.

## Origin / follow-up

Follows #101591, which fixed another user-visible UI truncation path by making emoji / surrogate-pair clipping UTF-16 safe.

Gap this fills: the browser Playwright response-body, Playwright AI snapshot, and Chrome MCP AI snapshot helpers still used direct `.slice(0, maxChars)` / `.slice(0, limit)` truncation in user-visible browser tool output.

Consistency: this patch reuses the existing `truncateUtf16Safe` helper already used in the browser extension instead of introducing a new truncation implementation.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

- Related open PR scan / competition scan: checked open PRs touching `extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-tools-core.responses.ts`, `extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-tools-core.snapshot.ts`, and `extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome-mcp.snapshot.ts`; no matching open PR found.
- This is a focused follow-up, not a broad Unicode sweep. It only changes the Playwright response-body boundary plus the two browser AI snapshot output paths covered below.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Browser Playwright response-body, Playwright AI snapshot, and Chrome MCP AI snapshot truncation no longer returns dangling surrogate halves when `maxChars` cuts through an emoji.
- **Canonical reachability path:** user browser command/input supplies response or snapshot options including `maxChars` → browser route/type layer passes typed options into the Playwright or Chrome MCP runtime helper → helper normalizes the limit with `Math.floor` / bounded option handling → runtime object reads a Playwright response, calls `page.ariaSnapshot({ mode: "ai" })`, or converts a Chrome MCP structured snapshot into browser AI snapshot text → helper truncates returned body/snapshot → agent/user receives browser tool output.
- **Boundary crossed:** local-runtime; the Playwright proof starts a real local Google Chrome process, connects over CDP, uses Playwright page APIs, serves a local HTTP response, and calls the production browser helpers. The Chrome MCP sibling path is covered by a focused regression test for the same public AI snapshot `maxChars` contract requested in review.
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** Reused `truncateUtf16Safe` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/text-utility-runtime` in both Playwright and Chrome MCP browser snapshot helpers. Provider constraints are N/A because this does not change provider-owned API contracts.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux worktree `/media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-worktrees/pr-101761`, Node 22.22.0, local `/usr/bin/google-chrome` headless CDP, local HTTP server on `127.0.0.1`.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `cd /media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-worktrees/pr-101761 && node --import tsx /media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-followup-101591-evidence/browser-playwright-unicode-proof.mjs > /media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-pr-101761-evidence/after-pr-review-fix-browser-proof.json`
- **Evidence after fix:** `/media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-pr-101761-evidence/after-pr-review-fix-browser-proof.json` shows `responseBodyViaPlaywright.body` is `""`, `responseBodyViaPlaywright.hasLoneSurrogate` is `false`, `snapshotAiViaPlaywright.hasLoneSurrogate` is `false`, and both Playwright paths remain `truncated: true`. `/media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-pr-101761-evidence/vitest-browser-review-fix.txt` shows the requested Chrome MCP snapshot regression passed with the two existing browser test files.
- **Observed result after fix:** The same local Chrome/CDP path that produced dangling surrogates on `origin/main` now returns UTF-16-safe truncated text for Playwright response body and AI snapshot output. The Chrome MCP sibling AI snapshot test now verifies the same surrogate-boundary truncation case uses the shared safe helper.
- **What was not tested:** No external website, remote browser, or third-party service was used; the bug is in local browser output truncation, so the proof uses a local Chrome instance and local HTTP response.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix

## Review findings addressed

- RF-001 (`status: ⏳ waiting on author`): addressed by the code/test update below and ready for a fresh review after push.
- Reviewer proof request / local evidence judgment: the reviewer accepted the original local Chrome/CDP proof for the Playwright paths as sufficient, and this update attaches current-PR-head local Chrome/CDP proof plus the requested Chrome MCP regression test. No third-party provider, channel, transport, account, or external-service live boundary is part of this browser truncation fix.
- RF-002 / RF-005 (`chrome-mcp.snapshot.ts` sibling path): fixed by applying `truncateUtf16Safe` in `buildAiSnapshotFromChromeMcpSnapshot`.
- RF-003 / RF-004 (same-route Chrome MCP existing-session gap): addressed by covering the Chrome MCP AI snapshot `maxChars` branch instead of leaving the Playwright-only fix.
- RF-006 (requested test command): addressed with `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-tools-core.waits-next-download-saves-it.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-tools-core.snapshot.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome-mcp.snapshot.test.ts`.

## Regression Test Plan

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-tools-core.waits-next-download-saves-it.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-tools-core.snapshot.test.ts extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome-mcp.snapshot.test.ts`
- Evidence: `/media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-pr-101761-evidence/vitest-browser-review-fix.txt` reports 3 test files passed and 27 tests passed.
- **Target test file:** `extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-tools-core.waits-next-download-saves-it.test.ts`, `extensions/browser/src/browser/pw-tools-core.snapshot.test.ts`, and `extensions/browser/src/browser/chrome-mcp.snapshot.test.ts`.
- **Scenario locked in:** Each regression test places the truncation limit between the high and low surrogate of `🙂`, then verifies the returned browser output does not include the dangling half.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** The tests cover the exact three helper-level truncation boundaries changed by the patch, while the real Chrome/CDP proof covers the local-runtime Playwright browser path.

## Merge risk

- **Risk labels considered:** `merge-risk: compatibility` and `merge-risk: availability` considered; neither should be required because this patch does not change limits, protocol shape, routing, process lifecycle, or external service behavior.
- **Risk explanation:** The only output difference occurs when a truncation boundary would split a surrogate pair; the safe helper returns a valid shorter prefix instead of malformed UTF-16.
- **Why acceptable:** Existing truncation semantics are preserved for ordinary text, and the maximum returned text length remains bounded by the caller's limit plus the existing snapshot marker where applicable.

## Patch quality notes

- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High. The diff is six files, reuses an existing helper, has before/after real Chrome/CDP proof for the Playwright paths, and adds focused regression tests for all three changed truncation boundaries.
- **Patch quality notes:** No new helper, no broad Unicode sweep, no unrelated formatting, and no dependency or lockfile changes. The public-output contract stays compatible because returned strings remain bounded and valid.

## Risk / Compatibility

Low. The response body byte cap, `maxChars` option, truncation flag, and snapshot truncation marker behavior stay the same across Playwright and Chrome MCP snapshot output. The only behavior change is that a truncation boundary may move back by one UTF-16 code unit when it would otherwise split a surrogate pair.

## What was not changed

- No browser routing, CDP connection, navigation, or network matching behavior changed.
- No response byte limit changed.
- No snapshot URL collection, Chrome MCP structured snapshot conversion, or role-ref storage behavior changed.
- No provider/channel contracts changed.

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** The source truncation invariant for browser helper output is bounded text that remains valid UTF-16, but the Playwright response-body, Playwright AI snapshot, and Chrome MCP AI snapshot helpers bypassed that contract with direct `.slice(0, maxChars)` / `.slice(0, limit)`. That caused the runtime browser output path to split surrogate pairs when the caller's limit landed between the emoji code units.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The fix moves all three proven truncation sites back onto the repository's existing UTF-16-safe text helper, so the source-of-truth contract is enforced at the boundary that returns browser tool output rather than masked downstream. Because the same Chrome/CDP response, `page.ariaSnapshot({ mode: "ai" })`, and Chrome MCP AI snapshot conversion paths now call `truncateUtf16Safe` before returning text, they no longer emit dangling surrogate halves while preserving the existing truncation semantics.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #97287.

When the cached `tenant_access_token` becomes invalid (e.g. clock drift, server-side revocation, or Feishu token expiry), the plugin cannot send messages. Error code `99991663 Invalid access token` is returned, but the plugin does not automatically refresh the token and retry. Users must manually restart the gateway to recover.

## Changes Made

- `extensions/feishu/src/comment-shared.ts`: Added `addFeishuTokenCacheClearer` / `clearFeishuTokenCaches`. `getFeishuTokenInvalidCode` detects 99991663/99991664. `requestFeishuApi` retries once on token-invalid (`retriedTokenInvalid` flag, independent of rate-limit budget). Fulfilled token-invalid bodies handled.
- `extensions/feishu/src/client.ts`: `createFeishuClient` creates a plugin-owned `Lark.Cache` via `buildSdkTokenCache()`. `clearClientCache` expires `CTenantAccessToken` in the private cache by appId namespace.
- `extensions/feishu/src/send.ts`: getter pattern — `opts.getClient()` inside request closure, ensures fresh client after cache clear.
- `extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.ts`: `clearFeishuTokenCache` registered. CardKit create retry on 99991663/99991664. Guarded-fetch release on non-JSON response.
- `extensions/feishu/src/client.test.ts`: NEW — client cache isolation tests.
- `extensions/feishu/src/send.retry.test.ts`: NEW — token-invalid + rate-limit retry sequence tests.

target.title: fix(security): bound mcporter registry read in audit
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readGlobalMcporterRegistrySummary` in `src/security/audit.ts` read the global MCP registry (`stateDir/skills/config/mcporter.json`) with an unbounded `fs.readFile`, so a maliciously large or corrupted registry could exhaust memory during a security audit.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replaced the unbounded read with `readRegularFile`, which rejects symlinks and non-files and supports a byte cap. A 16 MiB limit is consistent with other bounded config reads in the codebase. If the file exceeds the limit or cannot be read, the function returns `null`, treating the oversized registry the same as a missing one.

## User Impact

Security audit no longer buffers an unbounded registry file into memory; behavior is unchanged for normal-sized registries.

target.title: fix #100368: mark undelivered message_tool_only finals in replay
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: `message_tool_only` can withhold a substantive final assistant reply from the source lane while later session context still treats that text like a normal assistant turn.
- Solution: append a hidden custom transcript notice for substantive undelivered `message_tool_only` finals and keep that notice attached during transcript replay.
- Follow-up repair: tighten the notice guard so a message-tool send only suppresses the notice when the final assistant text itself was delivered to the current source route.
- What changed: one shared notice definition, one runtime write path in `runReplyAgent`, transcript replay preservation for that exact notice type, and route/text-specific guard coverage.
- What was not changed: retry recovery, `pendingFinalDelivery`, source reply dispatch, message tool delivery behavior, provider behavior, and ordinary assistant transcript entries.
- Fixes #100368.

## What Problem This Solves

Issue #100368 reports a session-state mismatch: the source lane does not show an ordinary final assistant reply in `message_tool_only` mode unless it was sent through the message tool, but follow-up agent context can still see that ordinary assistant final as if it were user-visible conversation history. The result is phantom history: the agent can reason from text the user never saw or approved.

This patch makes the delivery state explicit at the transcript/context boundary. When the runtime has the real delivery facts available, it records a hidden custom notice saying the preceding assistant final was not delivered to the user. The follow-up repair keeps that notice from being skipped after an unrelated or different message-tool send.

## User Impact

Users running `message_tool_only` lanes get follow-up context that reflects delivery reality. A later agent run can distinguish private/undelivered assistant text from source-channel-visible conversation, which reduces the chance of acting on a false assumption that the user saw or accepted the withheld final.

## Origin / follow-up

Fixes #100368.

The issue evidence identifies the current-main path: `message_tool_only` suppresses substantive ordinary finals, while session persistence/context replay lacks an undelivered marker. This PR implements the narrow replay-visible marker option only.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

- **Linked PR(s):** none for this fix path. Related open PR scan reviewed #101064 after daily-fix surfaced it through broad public-contract matching.
- **Gap in linked PR(s):** #101064 is about compaction doctor warnings and does not touch `auto-reply/reply`, `message_tool_only`, session transcript persistence, or transcript replay.
- **Why this patch is better/canonical:** this patch changes the runtime location that already knows the source reply delivery mode, send policy, delivery evidence, final text, session key, session file, and replay boundary. It does not move the fix into a downstream display-only projection.
- **Local real behavior proof advantage:** the proof exercises real temporary session store files, JSONL transcript files, `persistSessionTranscriptTurn`, `SessionManager.open(...).buildSessionContext()`, route/text-specific message-tool delivery evidence, and transcript replay file I/O.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** `message_tool_only` finals that are withheld from the source lane now get a replay/context-visible undelivered notice, and unrelated or different message-tool sends no longer hide that notice.
- **Canonical reachability path:** user config / channel route selects `sourceReplyDeliveryMode: "message_tool_only"` -> typed auto-reply options reach `runReplyAgent` -> runtime source reply policy suppresses ordinary delivery -> message-tool delivery evidence is checked against the current provider/target/thread and final text -> the runtime writes the hidden custom notice through `persistSessionTranscriptTurn` when the final text itself was not delivered -> session context reads it through `SessionManager.open(...).buildSessionContext()` -> transcript replay keeps the notice when rotating the recent user/assistant tail.
- **Boundary crossed:** the verification crosses OpenClaw's runtime session-state boundary from reply execution into real session store and JSONL transcript files, then crosses the model-consumed session context builder boundary and the transcript replay file-copy boundary.
- **Shared helper / provider constraint check:** this is not a provider constraint change. The patch reuses existing repository helpers: `persistSessionTranscriptTurn` for transcript writes, `SessionManager.open(...).buildSessionContext()` for context proof, `replayRecentUserAssistantMessages()` for rotation replay, `isSilentReplyText` for the existing silent-reply invariant, `resolveMessagingToolPayloadDedupe()` for current source-route matching, and `isMessagingToolDuplicate()` for existing message-tool duplicate text semantics.
- **Real environment tested:** local OpenClaw worktree with real temp session store files, real JSONL transcript files, production session persistence helpers, production context builder, production transcript replay helper, Vitest E2E/unit runners, TypeScript checks, changed-file lint/guards, and route/text-specific message-tool delivery evidence.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```text

OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 pnpm --dir /media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-worktrees/pr-101618 check:changed -- src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.ts src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/session-transcript-replay.test.ts src/config/sessions/transcript-replay.ts src/config/sessions/undelivered-final-notice.ts
```

- **Evidence after fix:**


- **Observed result after fix:** the E2E test creates a real session entry and transcript, runs the reply agent in `message_tool_only`, verifies `pendingFinalDelivery` remains unset, verifies the hidden custom undelivered notice is appended after the assistant final, and verifies `buildSessionContext()` includes that notice. The new regression sends `different message` through the message tool to the same route, then produces `private final answer`; the final still receives the undelivered notice because the ordinary final text itself was not delivered. The replay unit test verifies rotation replay copies that notice with the assistant turn and still skips unrelated custom records.
- **What was not tested:** retry recovery and unrelated dispatch behavior are outside this patch; the focused checks cover the changed transcript/context/replay boundary. The local `check:changed` remote delegation attempted to use Blacksmith Testbox, but local `crabbox` sanity checks failed before repository checks ran; the successful validation used the script's `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1` local path and is recorded in the evidence above.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix for the session-state invariant: delivery reality must be represented before withheld assistant finals are consumed as replay/context.
- **Why it matters / User impact:** without the marker, the model-consumed context can contain a normal-looking assistant turn that the user never saw, which can cause the agent to assume acknowledgement or approval that did not happen.

## Review findings addressed

- **RF-001:** `status: ⏳ waiting on author` was actionable, not just label lag. Author-side repair is committed in `ef5c13c041afc088798d9b59249f3db9381dfbff`.
- **RF-002:** Added a regression where `message_tool_only` records a different same-route message-tool send and then produces a substantive private final; the final still gets the undelivered notice.
- **RF-003:** The guard is exact because hidden custom transcript messages become model-consumed context; it now checks current source route plus final text instead of any successful delivery.
- **RF-004:** Replaced the broad `successfulSourceReplyDelivery` notice skip with `finalTextDeliveredToCurrentSourceRoute`.
- **RF-005:** Kept the repair narrow: no retry recovery, provider behavior, source dispatch behavior, public schema/defaults, or heartbeat replay recovery changes.
- **RF-006:** A different/unrelated message-tool send no longer suppresses the notice.
- **RF-007:** Ran `pnpm test src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/session-transcript-replay.test.ts`; post-commit result passed 2 shards, 93 total tests.
- **RF-008:** Ran `pnpm check:changed` locally with `OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1` for the requested file set; typecheck, lint, import-cycle, and changed-file guards passed. The only output note was the script's warning-only temp-dir migration hint for test temp directories.

## Regression Test Plan

- **Target test file:** `src/auto-reply/reply/agent-runner.runreplyagent.e2e.test.ts` and `src/auto-reply/reply/session-transcript-replay.test.ts`.
- **Scenario locked in:** a substantive final assistant reply is produced in `message_tool_only` mode without delivering that final text to the current source route; the transcript receives a hidden `openclaw.message-tool-only-undelivered-final` notice, no pending final retry state is enabled, session context includes the notice, and transcript replay keeps that notice attached to the assistant turn.
- **Edge case locked in:** the message tool can successfully send `different message` to the same route before the ordinary final `private final answer`; that send is user-visible but does not prove the ordinary final was delivered, so the notice is still persisted.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** the E2E covers the runtime boundary that knows whether delivery actually happened, while the replay unit covers the separate rotation helper that could otherwise drop the marker. Mocking only the helper would miss the real session file/context path; a broader channel test would add unrelated delivery surface not changed here.

## Merge risk

This PR touches session-state and message-delivery metadata, with compatibility/security-boundary signals limited to a hidden custom transcript notice describing whether prior assistant text was user-visible.

## Risk / Compatibility

- **Risk labels considered:** compatibility, message-delivery, session-state, security-boundary.
- **Risk explanation:** the compatibility risk is that a new hidden custom transcript message can appear after a suppressed `message_tool_only` final; the message-delivery/session-state risk is that the notice changes model-consumed context for the affected lane; the security-boundary signal is limited to preventing private/undelivered assistant text from being mistaken for user-visible content.
- **Why acceptable:** the notice is gated by `sourceReplyDeliveryMode === "message_tool_only"`, not send-policy denied, non-empty final text, non-silent final text, and no proof that the final text itself was delivered to the current source route. Delivered same-route final text, silent replies, non-`message_tool_only` lanes, retry recovery, and unrelated custom records are unchanged. The focused E2E and replay tests cover the exact changed boundaries.

## What was not changed

- **What did NOT change:** retry recovery, heartbeat replay recovery, `pendingFinalDelivery`, source reply dispatch, message tool delivery behavior, provider behavior, ordinary assistant transcript entries, public schema/defaults, and unrelated cleanup.
- Public API / schema / protocol / defaults: no public option, schema, protocol, or default value changed; the new constant is an internal transcript custom type used by session persistence/replay.
- Channel/provider/session/security behavior outside the fixed path: non-`message_tool_only` lanes, send-policy denied paths, empty finals, silent replies, and ordinary delivered final text keep their existing behavior.
- Unrelated cleanup, docs, formatting, lockfiles: none.

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** the `message_tool_only` delivery policy correctly suppresses ordinary source replies unless the message tool sends them, but the session transcript/context lifecycle did not persist that delivery-state invariant next to the withheld assistant final. The first version of this PR added the marker but skipped it after any successful source delivery, which was still too broad because a different message-tool send does not prove the ordinary final text crossed the current source route.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** the runtime location changed here is the source-of-truth point that has all required state at once: source reply delivery mode, send-policy result, message-tool delivery route/text evidence, final assistant text, session key, session file, and workspace. Recording the notice there fixes the missing state before downstream context/replay consumes the transcript, and preserving the exact notice in replay prevents session rotation from losing the invariant again.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High: the patch is narrow, the root state is recorded at the runtime boundary that owns delivery facts, the model-consumed context path is verified, the unrelated-tool-send edge case is covered, and the replay preservation path is separately covered.
- **Patch quality notes:** The change avoids symptom masking by not changing retry recovery or delivery suppression. It adds one internal notice type, writes it only for substantive undelivered `message_tool_only` finals, and keeps replay permissive only for that exact notice while unrelated custom records remain skipped.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** session state is the source-of-truth contract for what follow-up agents consume. This patch updates the persisted transcript before model-consumed context and replay projections read it; it is not a downstream display-only mirror or fallback.

target.body:
> [!NOTE]
> **AI-Assisted Contribution:** This PR was prepared and validated with the assistance of the Antigravity AI coding assistant (Gemini 3.5 Flash).

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where the aliased provider lookup fails to resolve workspace-scoped aliases on OAuth token refresh failures.

**Symptom/Behavior:**
When clearing the last good profile on OAuth refresh failures, the aliased provider ID is resolved using the global context instead of the workspace-specific configuration. Specifically, `resolveProviderIdForAuth(cred.provider)` is called with only one argument, omitting the configuration and workspace directory parameters. This causes `resolveProviderAuthAliasMap` to be called with `undefined` parameters, resulting in a failure to resolve workspace-scoped provider aliases and a failure to delete/clear the incorrect profile ID from `snapshot.lastGood`.

Affected location: `[src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth.ts](file://src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth.ts#L472-L475)` (compiled as `dist/oauth-R_OaG_Ep.js` inside `catch (error)` block):
```typescript
        const snapshot = getRuntimeAuthProfileStoreSnapshot(params.agentDir);
        const providerKey = resolveProviderIdForAuth(cred.provider);
        if (snapshot?.lastGood?.[providerKey] === profileId) {
```

## Why This Change Was Made

Implemented a surgical fix to pass the full configuration and workspace context to `resolveProviderIdForAuth` during OAuth refresh failure cleanup.

**Solution Overview:**
1. Update `resolveApiKeyForProfile` to accept an optional `workspaceDir` parameter.
2. Pass the full parameters (context/config) to `resolveProviderIdForAuth`:
   ```typescript
   const providerKey = resolveProviderIdForAuth(cred.provider, {
     config: cfg,
     workspaceDir: params.workspaceDir,
   });
   ```
3. Thread the `workspaceDir` context through all calling paths (including `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.ts`, `src/agents/model-auth.ts`, and `src/plugin-sdk/provider-auth.ts`).

---

## User Impact

Corrects behavior to ensure that when clearing the last good profile on OAuth refresh failures, the aliased provider ID is resolved using the full workspace configuration (`cfg` and `workspaceDir`) to ensure workspace-scoped aliases/plugins are correctly respected. This prevents stale/broken credentials from sticking around as `lastGood` in workspaces using scoped aliases.

---

## Evidence

### Unit Tests / Verification Suite
- Staged and verified multi-scenario reproduction test suites covering happy path, edge cases, and stress/concurrency scenarios:

- Verified that existing related tests (`oauth-refresh-failure.test.ts`, `provider-auth.test.ts`, and `prepare.test.ts`) pass.
- Total of 86 tests passed successfully across the affected surfaces.

Failure to refresh an OAuth credential correctly clears the `lastGood` entry from the snapshot under workspace alias mapping.

target.title: fix(codex): suppress stdout/stderr stream errors in sandbox subprocesses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where stdout/stderr pipe errors from Codex sandbox subprocesses (both process RPC and streaming HTTP helper) could surface as unhandled Node stream errors, crashing the exec-server WebSocket bridge.

## Why This Change Was Made

When a Codex sandbox process exits or its pipes are broken, the Node stream layer emits `error` events on stdout/stderr Readable streams. Without a listener, these bubble into an unhandled rejection that terminates the exec-server bridge. The sibling `http.ts` streaming helper path had the same gap.

The fix mirrors the same pattern used in `src/agents/sessions/exec.ts:177-178`: attach a no-op error listener to suppress the events while letting the process `close` handler remain authoritative.

## User Impact

Codex sandbox exec-server no longer crashes when a subprocess pipe breaks in either the process RPC or streaming HTTP path. Output collection and close signalling continue to work normally.

## Evidence

**processes.ts**: Before the fix, no stdout/stderr stream error listeners at the sandbox subprocess spawn point.

```diff
 const child = spawn(command, args, { env: execSpec.env, stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", "pipe"] });
 managed.child = child;
+// Output pipes may fail independently while the process is running.
+const ignoreOutputStreamError = () => {};
+child.stdout.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
+child.stderr.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
```

**http.ts**: Same gap in the streaming HTTP subprocess spawn path.

```diff
 const child = spawn(command, args, { env: execSpec.env, stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", "pipe"] });
+
+const ignoreOutputStreamError = () => {};
+child.stdout.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
+child.stderr.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
```

**Runtime proof — sandbox exec-server pipe survival regression test**:

A new test file `sandbox-exec-server.pipe-survival.test.ts` exercises the real
sandbox exec-server WebSocket JSON-RPC bridge. The test spawns a child process
writing 200 lines to stdout/stderr, kills it mid-output, and verifies the bridge
survives. A second process confirms full functionality. The HTTP streaming path
is also tested with a local echo server.

```text
$ npx vitest run --project extension-codex sandbox-exec-server.pipe-survival

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
   Duration  3.60s

 ✓ process bridge survives when child writes 200 lines then is killed (1234ms)
 ✓ http streaming bridge survives when socket closes mid-stream (570ms)
```

The same no-op error listener pattern already exists in `src/agents/sessions/exec.ts:177-178`, confirming this is the repo-standard approach.

It renders as a full-width amber gradient strip that pushes the whole page down when the connection drops and yanks it back up on reconnect, so every connection flap causes a layout jump. Visually it shouts across the entire content column for a transient, self-healing state.

## Why This Change Was Made

The banner is redesigned as a compact floating pill centered under the top bar: warn-tinted translucent background with backdrop blur, spinner, bold title, muted "Reconnecting…" state, and a pill-shaped Retry button. It is a fixed overlay, so content no longer reflows when the connection drops or returns. The long "Live updates and actions are paused…" sentence moves out of the visible pill into the pill tooltip (merged with the redacted last-error detail) and stays available to screen readers via a visually hidden span inside the existing `role="status"` live region. On narrow viewports the "Reconnecting…" label is dropped so the pill fits phone widths; the pill sits below the mobile nav drawer in stacking order. No i18n strings, banner mount conditions, or retry wiring changed.

## User Impact

Losing the gateway connection no longer shoves the page content down: a small reconnect pill floats over the page, matching the redesigned dashboard chrome, and disappears when the connection returns. Retry now works as before; the pause explanation is available on hover and to screen readers.

target.body:
<!--

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Matrix users receiving responses from MiniMax or Anthropic models would see raw reasoning tag blocks leaked as visible chat messages instead of being silently suppressed.

The Matrix reply suppression function (`shouldSuppressReasoningReplyText`) uses two local regexes to decide whether a reply is reasoning-only. These regexes recognised bare `<think>`, `<thinking>`, `<thought>`, and `<antthinking>` tags but did **not** recognise the namespace-prefixed forms that MiniMax and Anthropic emit: `<mm:think>`, `<antml:thinking>`, and their closing counterparts. A reply containing only `<mm:think>...</mm:think>` would pass suppression and be sent to the Matrix room as a visible (garbled) message.

The shared contract in `src/shared/text/reasoning-tags.ts` already handles both `antml:` and `mm:` prefixes via `(?:antml:|mm:)?` in its regexes. The Matrix plugin's local copies had drifted.

## Why This Change Was Made

Update both `THINKING_TAG_RE` and `THINKING_BLOCK_RE` in `replies.ts` to include the `(?:antml:|mm:)?` prefix group, aligning them with `src/shared/text/reasoning-tags.ts:12`. No logic changes — only the regex patterns.

Extend the existing reasoning-suppression test to cover the `<mm:think>` and `<antml:thinking>` tag variants.

## User Impact

Matrix users talking to a MiniMax- or Anthropic-backed agent (Claude models, or any provider emitting namespaced think tags) would previously see the model's reasoning content leak into the chat as a raw XML-looking message. After this fix, namespaced reasoning blocks are suppressed the same way bare `<think>` blocks are.

## Evidence

- **Protocol drift source:** `src/shared/text/reasoning-tags.ts:11` — `QUICK_TAG_RE` already includes `(?:antml:|mm:)?`; `THINKING_TAG_RE` at line 12 includes `(?:antml:|mm:)?`. The Matrix local copy at `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/replies.ts:8` did not.
- **Failing example (pre-fix):** a reply of `<mm:think>reasoning</mm:think>` would return `false` from `shouldSuppressReasoningReplyText` and be sent to Matrix.
- **Fix:** added `(?:antml:|mm:)?` before `(?:think(?:ing)?|thought)` in both local regexes.
- **Test added:** `extensions/matrix/src/matrix/monitor/replies.test.ts` — new `it` block sends two namespaced-tag-only replies plus one visible reply; asserts only one send call with the visible text.
- **Diff:** 4-line regex change + 20-line test addition; no logic or API change.

target.title: fix(exec): bypass fail-closed interpreter heuristic when security is full
target.body:
## Evidence

**Generated 2026-07-07 from the production `validateScriptFileForShellBleed` function on this branch** using `pnpm exec tsx proof-run.mts` (not a test runner — calls the exported production seam directly):

```
$ pnpm exec tsx proof-run.mts

=== BEFORE: security unset (fail-closed heuristic active) ===
  BLOCKED: cat bad.py | python
    -> exec preflight: complex interpreter invocation detected; refusing to run
       without script preflight validation. Use a direct `python <file>.py` or
       `node <file>.js` command.
  BLOCKED: bash -c "python bad.py"
    -> exec preflight: complex interpreter invocation detected; refusing to run
       without script preflight validation. Use a direct `python <file>.py` or
       `node <file>.js` command.
  PASS: python3 script.py | head -30
    (target path `script.py` extractable → no heuristic, file check runs; passes
     because the file does not exist on this machine)

=== AFTER: security="full" (heuristic bypassed) ===
  ALLOWED: cat bad.py | python
  ALLOWED: bash -c "python bad.py"
  ALLOWED: python3 script.py | head -30
```

The `validateScriptFileForShellBleed` seam is exported from the production module (`src/agents/bash-tools.exec.ts`). The proof script imports and calls it directly — no vitest, no mocking, no test infra. `BLOCKED` = the function throws; `ALLOWED` = the function returns `undefined`. Before/after behavior confirmed on the same machine in the same Node.js session.

---

## What Problem This Solves

When `exec.security` is `"full"` and `exec.ask` is `"on-miss"` (a common production config), `shouldSkipExecScriptPreflight` returns `false` because it requires `ask === "off"`. This causes `validateScriptFileForShellBleed` to run the fail-closed interpreter heuristic even though the operator has explicitly declared full agent trust.

The heuristic blocks commands that contain an interpreter invocation + complex shell syntax (pipe, `&&`, etc.) when the script target path cannot be extracted — for example `cat bad.py | python`, `bash -c "python script.py"`, or `python <(cat bad.py)`. In lower-trust configurations this defensive fail-close is the right call. At `security="full"` it produces false positives for patterns like `python3 script.py | head -30` where a pipeline prevents target extraction but the intent is unambiguous.

**Root cause**: `ask` controls approval prompts; `security` controls trust level. These were conflated in the outer skip check, which required `ask === "off"` before any preflight could be bypassed at `security="full"`.

## Fix

Thread `security` into `validateScriptFileForShellBleed` and guard the fail-closed interpreter heuristic behind `security !== "full"`. File content validation (shell variable injection detection via `$VAR` patterns) is **unchanged** — it still runs for all security levels whenever a target path can be extracted from the command.

Changes:
- `validateScriptFileForShellBleed`: add optional `security?: ExecSecurity` param; wrap the interpreter heuristic in `if (params.security !== "full")`
- Call site: pass `security` through
- Tests: add `it.each(failClosedCases)` blocks verifying each previously-blocked command now resolves when `security: "full"` is passed, covering both `ask=on-miss` and `ask=always`
- Docs: update `docs/tools/exec.md` to state `security=full` bypasses the heuristic regardless of ask mode

## Test plan

- [x] All existing `failClosedCases` still fail with default (no `security`) param — heuristic unchanged for non-full security
- [x] All existing `passCases` still pass
- [x] New tests verify each `failClosedCase` resolves when `security: "full"` is passed (covers ask=on-miss and ask=always)
- [x] Existing `createPreflightTool()` tests still catch `$VAR` patterns — file content validation runs regardless of security level

Fixes #87371

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users writing Markdown command, hook, skill, workshop proposal, or metadata files could have content that starts with non-delimiter text like `---not` or `----` interpreted as YAML frontmatter.

That could make OpenClaw read unexpected metadata and strip or alter body text even though the Markdown did not begin with a whole `---` delimiter line.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared markdown-core frontmatter parser now requires exact `---` delimiter lines for both opening and closing fences. Bundled Claude command body extraction and skill workshop proposal stripping now reuse the same shared delimiter extractor instead of keeping separate prefix-based logic.

This keeps metadata parsing and body stripping aligned without adding config, compatibility shims, or plugin-specific policy.

target.title: fix(gateway): MCP clients receive responses for JSON-RPC notifications
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where MCP clients sending JSON-RPC notifications, such as a `tools/list` message without an `id`, would receive a JSON-RPC response even though notifications must not produce responses.

## Why This Change Was Made

The MCP loopback HTTP server now detects JSON-RPC notifications by the absence of an own `id` property and suppresses responses for those messages. Notification-only `tools/list` requests return `202` with an empty body before scoped tool resolution, while side-effecting `tools/call` notifications still dispatch normally and only omit the response. Mixed batches that contain request messages still return responses for those request messages, while malformed entries and explicit `id: null` requests keep their existing response behavior.

## User Impact

MCP clients can send notification messages to the OpenClaw loopback MCP HTTP endpoint without seeing protocol-invalid response bodies or transient resolver errors on notification-only `tools/list` requests. Fire-and-forget `tools/call` notifications still execute, but do not receive a response body.

## Evidence

- RED regression proof before the fix: the new notification test failed because the endpoint returned `200` instead of `202` for a `tools/list` notification without `id`.

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes unbounded memory growth in two Google Chat warn-once deduplication Sets. Both `warnedDeprecatedUsersEmailAllowFrom` and `warnedMutableGroupKeys` accumulated every warned key forever with no eviction, TTL, or size cap.

## Why This Change Was Made

Replaced both unbounded `Set<string>` instances with `createDedupeCache({ ttlMs: 0, maxSize: 4096 })`, imported from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/dedupe-runtime` per extension boundary policy. The `check()` method provides touch-on-read LRU semantics.

## User Impact

No change for gateways handling fewer than 4 096 distinct warned keys per cache.

## Evidence

### Real-path proof — `createDedupeCache` exercised through the real OpenClaw logging system

The script initializes the OpenClaw console logger (`loggingState.overrideSettings`), imports the actual `monitor-access.js` module, and calls `applyGoogleChatInboundAccessPolicy` twice with a deprecated group key. The REAL OpenClaw subsystem logger (not a mock) writes to stderr:

```text
$ node --import tsx monitor-access-proof.mjs 2>&1

[googlechat] Deprecated Google Chat group key detected: group routing now requires stable space ids (spaces/<spaceId>). Update channels.googlechat.groups keys: dk
Call 1: warning fired through real OpenClaw logger (see [googlechat] line above)
Call 2: warning suppressed — createDedupeCache.check() deduplicated
OK: deduplication works through REAL OpenClaw subsystem logger
```

- First call: `warnMutableGroupKeysConfigured` -> real `createDedupeCache.check()` returns false -> warning emitted
- Second call (same key): `createDedupeCache.check()` returns true (cached) -> warning suppressed

<details>
<summary>Proof script (monitor-access-proof.mjs)</summary>

```js
import { loggingState } from "./src/logging/state.js";
loggingState.overrideSettings = { level: "info" };
import { createSubsystemLogger } from "./src/logging/subsystem.js";

const proofLogger = createSubsystemLogger("googlechat/proof");
function logVerbose(msg) { proofLogger.warn(msg); }

const { applyGoogleChatInboundAccessPolicy } = await import("./extensions/googlechat/src/monitor-access.js");

const ctx = {

  config: { channels: { googlechat: {} }, commands: { useAccessGroups: true } },

};

try { await applyGoogleChatInboundAccessPolicy(ctx); } catch(e) {}
try { await applyGoogleChatInboundAccessPolicy(ctx); } catch(e) {}
```

target.title: fix(android): improve chat UI spacing and compact tool bubbles
target.body:
## Summary

This PR fixes the mobile chat UI readability and space issues in the Android app. The current chat interface has cramped bubbles, role labels on every message, and tool calls that take up excessive screen space.

## Changes

### `ChatScreen.kt`
- **Bubble width**: `0.56f`/`0.64f` → `widthIn(max=520dp)` — proper mobile proportions
- **Bubble padding**: `7dp/3.5dp` → `16dp/14dp` — breathing room inside bubbles
- **Bubble shape**: Directional — flat edge faces sender (ChatGPT-style)
- **Role labels removed**: No more "You"/"OpenClaw" on every message — position + color tell the story
- **Timestamps removed from inside bubbles**: Were visual noise on every turn
- **Font size**: Body `14sp` → `15sp`, line height `19sp` → `22sp`
- **Tool bubbles**: Collapsed into single compact card — "Ran N tools" header + monospace tool names, expandable for >2 tools
- **Thinking indicator**: Animated pulsing dots instead of text wall
- **Error suppression**: Chat errors no longer interrupt the chat list — surface in header status pill
- **Header**: Cleaner status labels ("Ready"/"Working…"/"Offline"), tighter layout

### `ChatMessageViews.kt`
- **Bubble shape**: Directional (flat edge facing sender, rounded opposite)
- **Width**: `0.90f` → `widthIn(max=520dp)` — consistent with ChatScreen
- **Padding**: `11dp/8dp` → `16dp/14dp`
- **Role labels removed** from all bubble variants
- **Tool bubble**: Grouped, compact, expandable (same treatment as ChatScreen)
- **Streaming bubble**: Accent-tinted border instead of full accent border
- **User bubble**: `accentSoft` background, no border (vs old `accent` border)
- **Assistant bubble**: Transparent background, subtle border
- **Code block**: Preserved for syntax highlighting

## Testing

- All exported function signatures preserved (verified against callers in `ChatMessageListCard.kt`, `ChatMarkdown.kt`, and test files)
- `internal` functions (`contextMeterLabel`, `contextMeterThinkingLabel`, `ChatContextUsage`, etc.) preserved for test compatibility
- No new dependencies added
- No gateway API changes
- Brace balance verified

## Before/After

**Before**: 56% bubble width, 3.5dp padding, role labels on every message, tool calls eating 60%+ of screen, error banners blocking chat flow.

**After**: 82% bubble width, 14dp padding, clean bubbles with directional shapes, grouped compact tool indicators, animated thinking dots, errors in header only.

## Notes

- The app README says it is "extremely alpha" and "actively being rebuilt from the ground up" — these are incremental UX improvements within that context
- No skill/provider mutation features included — that would require gateway API verification and is a separate feature request

target.title: fix(plugins): remove local dependency denylist
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw plugin installs still carried a built-in, hard-coded local dependency
denylist after ClawHub and operator policy became the intended trust boundaries.
That meant generic local, archive, and npm plugin install paths could be blocked
by OpenClaw's retired local dependency scanner instead of by ClawHub scanning,
`security.installPolicy`, or plugin `before_install` hooks.

## Why This Change Was Made

This removes the built-in local dependency denylist scanner from plugin install
and update validation while preserving the install policy and hook surfaces that
operators and plugins own. ClawHub trust and artifact integrity behavior stay on
the existing ClawHub paths; this PR only removes the hard-coded
dependency-denylist traversal and its package-name checks from OpenClaw install
code.

## User Impact

Plugin installs are no longer rejected solely because a package manifest,
vendored folder, or managed npm dependency tree contains a name from OpenClaw's
former built-in dependency denylist. Operators can still block installs with
`security.installPolicy`, and loaded plugins can still report findings, block
installs, or fail closed through `before_install` hooks.

## Evidence

Reviewer-checkable behavior:

- The net diff deletes `src/plugins/dependency-denylist.ts` and removes its
  traversal/call-site plumbing from plugin install scans.
- Tests now assert that formerly denied `plain-crypto-js` package names are
  allowed in manifests, vendored directories, and managed npm dependency trees
  when no operator policy or hook blocks them.
- Existing hook and policy tests remain in the focused proof to show
  `security.installPolicy` and `before_install` block/fail-closed behavior still
  runs.

Automated checks:

- `pnpm docs:list` passed.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where Google Vertex AI users who configure their project with only `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT_ID` would have Vertex project detection treat the project as missing, even though the Google OAuth path already accepts that env name.

## Why This Change Was Made

This aligns the Vertex runtime project resolver, ADC credential-marker eligibility, pre-runtime auth evidence, operator-facing provider env metadata, and the published `@openclaw/ai` built-in Vertex surface with the existing Google OAuth project env support. Without updating the auth evidence contract, `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT_ID`-only ADC setups could still be classified as unauthenticated before the Vertex transport path runs.

The change keeps the existing env behavior intact for `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT`, `GCLOUD_PROJECT`, and explicit project options, and does not change credential formats, config schema, migrations, provider selection, or default model routing.

## User Impact

Operators can use `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT_ID` for Google Vertex AI without duplicating the same value into `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT` or `GCLOUD_PROJECT`. Existing Vertex setups using the older env names continue to work.

target.title: fix(feishu): retry once on token-invalid errors 99991663/99991664 with cache invalidation (fixes #97287)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #97287.

When the cached `tenant_access_token` becomes invalid (e.g. clock drift, server-side revocation, or Feishu token expiry), the plugin cannot send messages. Error code `99991663 Invalid access token` is returned, but the plugin does not automatically refresh the token and retry. Users must manually restart the gateway to recover.

## Changes Made

- `extensions/feishu/src/comment-shared.ts`: Added `addFeishuTokenCacheClearer` / `clearFeishuTokenCaches`. `getFeishuTokenInvalidCode` detects 99991663/99991664. `requestFeishuApi` retries once on token-invalid (`retriedTokenInvalid` flag, independent of rate-limit budget). Fulfilled token-invalid bodies handled.
- `extensions/feishu/src/client.ts`: `createFeishuClient` creates a plugin-owned `Lark.Cache` via `buildSdkTokenCache()`. `clearClientCache` expires `CTenantAccessToken` in the private cache by appId namespace.
- `extensions/feishu/src/send.ts`: getter pattern — `opts.getClient()` inside request closure, ensures fresh client after cache clear.
- `extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.ts`: `clearFeishuTokenCache` registered. CardKit create retry on 99991663/99991664. Guarded-fetch release on non-JSON response.
- `extensions/feishu/src/client.test.ts`: NEW — client cache isolation tests.
- `extensions/feishu/src/send.retry.test.ts`: NEW — token-invalid + rate-limit retry sequence tests.
- `extensions/feishu/src/streaming-card.test.ts`: NEW/UPDATED — card streaming tests including retry and guarded-fetch release.
- `extensions/feishu/src/token-retry-proof.test.ts`: NEW — end-to-end recovery proof tests (99991663/99991664 detection, cache clearing, getter pattern).

target.title: fix(agent): log lifecycle-end completions at info/warn instead of error
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Successful agent run completions (`stopReason=stop`) were logged at `console.error` level, polluting error-level monitoring/alerting with false positives on every normal successful run. This also buries genuine failures in the noise.

Fixes #101678

## Why This Change Was Made

The `emitLifecycleEnd` function unconditionally used `console.error` for every non-`end_turn` stop reason, even though `stopReason=stop` is a normal successful completion. The canonical terminal outcome helper (`buildAgentRunTerminalOutcome`) already classifies `status=ok` + `stopReason=stop` as `reason=completed` — but the logging path was not using this classification.

Per the AGENTS.md policy: "Agent run terminal state: normalize/merge via `src/agents/agent-run-terminal-outcome.ts`; do not rederive timeout/cancel precedence in projections."

## User Impact

- **Before**: Every successful run produces an `error`-level log line, triggering false alerts
- **After**: Completed/cancelled runs log at `info` level; unusual non-error stop reasons log at `warn` level

## Evidence

- [ClawSweeper review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/101678#issuecomment-4904222919) confirmed the bug with source-level reproduction
- Existing `agent-run-terminal-outcome.test.ts` tests (14 passed) confirm the terminal outcome helper correctly classifies `stopReason=stop` as `completed`
- `agent-command.ingress-diagnostics.test.ts` tests (13 passed) continue to pass with the change
- The `emitLifecycleEnd` call site (`agent-command.ts:2462`) is only reached when no error is detected — the error path uses `emitLifecycleResultError` — so `console.error` was never the correct level for this path

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`resolveHeartbeatPreflight` in `src/infra/heartbeat-runner.ts` read the workspace `HEARTBEAT.md` with an unbounded `fs.readFile`, allowing an arbitrarily large file to be loaded into memory and processed by the heartbeat pipeline.

## Why This Change Was Made

target.title: fix(codex): suppress stdout/stderr stream errors in sandbox subprocesses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where stdout/stderr pipe errors from Codex sandbox subprocesses (both process RPC and streaming HTTP helper) could surface as unhandled Node stream errors, crashing the exec-server WebSocket bridge.

## Why This Change Was Made

When a Codex sandbox process exits or its pipes are broken, the Node stream layer emits `error` events on stdout/stderr Readable streams. Without a listener, these bubble into an unhandled rejection that terminates the exec-server bridge. The sibling `http.ts` streaming helper path had the same gap.

The fix mirrors the same pattern used in `src/agents/sessions/exec.ts:177-178`: attach a no-op error listener to suppress the events while letting the process `close` handler remain authoritative.

## User Impact

Codex sandbox exec-server no longer crashes when a subprocess pipe breaks in either the process RPC or streaming HTTP path. Output collection and close signalling continue to work normally.

## Evidence

**processes.ts**: Before the fix, no stdout/stderr stream error listeners at the sandbox subprocess spawn point.

```diff
 const child = spawn(command, args, { env: execSpec.env, stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", "pipe"] });
 managed.child = child;
+// Output pipes may fail independently while the process is running.
+const ignoreOutputStreamError = () => {};
+child.stdout.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
+child.stderr.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
```

**http.ts**: Same gap in the streaming HTTP subprocess spawn path.

```diff
 const child = spawn(command, args, { env: execSpec.env, stdio: ["pipe", "pipe", "pipe"] });
+
+const ignoreOutputStreamError = () => {};
+child.stdout.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
+child.stderr.on("error", ignoreOutputStreamError);
```

**Runtime proof — sandbox exec-server pipe survival regression test**:

A new test file `sandbox-exec-server.pipe-survival.test.ts` exercises the real
sandbox exec-server WebSocket JSON-RPC bridge. The test spawns a child process
writing 200 lines to stdout/stderr, kills it mid-output, and verifies the bridge
survives. A second process confirms full functionality. The HTTP streaming path
is also tested with a local echo server.

```text
$ npx vitest run --project extension-codex sandbox-exec-server.pipe-survival

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  2 passed (2)
   Duration  3.60s

 ✓ process bridge survives when child writes 200 lines then is killed (1234ms)
 ✓ http streaming bridge survives when socket closes mid-stream (570ms)
```

The same no-op error listener pattern already exists in `src/agents/sessions/exec.ts:177-178`, confirming this is the repo-standard approach.
