## What Problem This Solves

`swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit` fails on any Mac where the OpenClaw app previously paired: `GatewayNodeSessionTests` "non bootstrap hello stores primary device token but not additional bootstrap tokens" and "untrusted bootstrap hello does not persist bootstrap handoff tokens" expect `DeviceAuthStore.loadToken` to return nil, but real operator/node device tokens leak into the per-test state dirs. CI (clean machines) passes, so the breakage only hits local development.

Root cause is in prod code, not the tests: `DeviceIdentityStore.loadOrCreate(profile:)` passes `DeviceIdentityPaths.appGroupMigrationSource(profile:)`, which on unentitled processes (test runners, the shipped mac app) points at the machine's real app-group container. Any fresh state dir has no identity file, so `migratedIdentity` copies the machine's real `device.json` and `device-auth.json` — real device tokens included — into every `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR`-overridden temp dir. That contradicts the function's own contract comment ("only for builds whose store selection fell back to legacy storage"): an explicit override is not the legacy fallback.

## Why This Change Was Made

- `DeviceIdentityPaths.appGroupMigrationSource` now returns nil when `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` is set (new `stateDirOverridden` parameter on the injectable variant), honoring the documented legacy-fallback-only contract. Overridden stores (tests, relocated installs) no longer silently import the machine's real pairing identity and tokens.
- `StateDirectoryIsolationTrait` now owns test state-dir isolation instead of only serializing: it pins `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` to a fresh temp dir per gated test and afterwards restores the launch value or a run-scoped quarantine dir — never unset — so stray late writes from leaked reconnect tasks cannot reach the developer's real store. The identical 14-line setenv/defer block is deleted from 12 tests; net diff is +76/-191.

## User Impact

- Local `swift test` runs of OpenClawKit pass regardless of machine pairing state, and tests can no longer read or overwrite a developer's real device-auth store (the old behavior could clobber a real node token with a test literal).
- Product behavior change is narrow: unentitled builds running with an explicit `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` override no longer import app-group container identity into the override dir. Default store selection (container/legacy) is unchanged.

## Evidence

- After fix: `swift test --package-path apps/shared/OpenClawKit --filter "GatewayNodeSessionTests|DeviceIdentityStoreTests"` passes 44/44 on the same polluted Mac, including the new regression test "provides no app group migration source when the state dir is overridden".

target.title: fix(approvals): identify the originating session in approval prompts
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Channel-delivered approval prompts (exec and plugin) identify the requesting *agent* (`Agent: main`) but not the *session*. An operator who runs several concurrent sessions of the same agent — a main chat session, a subagent, a cron/heartbeat instance — receives approval prompts that are visually indistinguishable except by whatever the command text happens to reveal. Approving the wrong session's request is exactly the failure mode approval prompts exist to prevent. The session key is already computed and already travels on the delivered payload envelope (`channelData.execApproval.sessionKey`) for programmatic reply-routing — it is simply dropped from the human-readable text (`buildExecApprovalRequestMessage` never reads `request.request.sessionKey`).

Related, but a different surface: #9876 asks for session context in the macOS native approval popup (needs-product-decision). This PR only touches the channel chat text and its metadata envelope, where the value already flows.

## Why This Change Was Made

Approval prompts render through four layers, and this PR covers each with a null-conditional Session field (per ClawSweeper's review, the first revision only covered the generic fallback text — adapter-backed/native prompts were repaired in follow-up commits):

- **Generic fallback text**: `buildExecApprovalRequestMessage` (`src/infra/exec-approval-forwarder.ts`) and `buildPluginApprovalRequestMessage` (`src/infra/plugin-approvals.ts`) render `Session: <sessionKey>` after the existing `Agent:` line.
- **Structured adapter prompts** (Slack/Google Chat/Discord/Matrix render `view.metadata` rows): `buildExecMetadata`/`buildPluginMetadata` in `src/infra/approval-view-model.ts` add a `Session` row; `PluginApprovalViewBase` now carries `sessionKey` like the exec view already did.
- **Native/forwarded pending payloads** (Telegram/iMessage/Matrix native + telegram forwarding): `buildExecApprovalPendingReplyPayload` (`src/infra/exec-approval-reply.ts`) renders a `Session:` info line; the Telegram native adapter and `buildTelegramExecApprovalPendingPayload` now pass `agentId`/`sessionKey` through (they previously dropped both), and the Matrix native plugin branch threads `sessionKey` when reconstructing the request from the view.
- **Reaction-native prompts** (WhatsApp/Signal) and **QQBot's local text builders**: `buildApprovalReactionPromptText` (`src/plugin-sdk/approval-reaction-runtime.ts`) and `buildExecApprovalText`/`buildPluginApprovalText` (`extensions/qqbot/src/engine/approval/index.ts`) render the same Session field.

Envelope parity, per review: `buildPluginApprovalPendingReplyPayload` (`src/plugin-sdk/approval-renderers.ts`) now mirrors `sessionKey`/`agentId` onto the plugin pending payload's metadata envelope the way the exec path already does, so rendered text and `channelData` never diverge. Deliberately untouched: the deterministic in-session prompt (`embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.tools.ts`) renders inside the very session that owns the approval, so session disambiguation there adds noise.

No routing, policy, or approval-decision changes; prompts without a session key render exactly as before.

## User Impact

An operator juggling several sessions of one agent can now see which session is asking before approving (`Session: agent:main:telegram:direct:…` under the `Agent:` line, in both exec and plugin approval prompts). Channel bots and native wrappers that consume the metadata envelope get the same identity fields for plugin approvals that they already had for exec approvals.

## Evidence

HEAD: `7f7de2bdb1612fab37583e1ac442e8a88409c457` (base upstream/main `68e06b9ea1`)

Real behavior proof (production prompt builders, no mocks; captured at this HEAD):

```
=== production exec approval prompt (session present) ===
🔒 Exec approval required
ID: req-1
Command: `rm -rf build`
CWD: /home/user/project
Host: gateway
Agent: main
Session: agent:main:telegram:direct:424242
Security: allowlist
...

=== session omitted (no sessionKey on request) ===
Agent: main

=== production plugin approval prompt (session present) ===
🛡️ Plugin approval required
Title: Sensitive tool call
...
Agent: main
Session: agent:main:telegram:direct:424242
```

Focused tests (all green locally at this HEAD):

- `src/infra/exec-approval-forwarder.test.ts` — Session rendered when present; omitted when the request carries no session key
- `src/infra/plugin-approval-forwarder.test.ts` — forwarded plugin approval text contains the Session line AND the delivered `channelData.execApproval` envelope carries the same `sessionKey`/`agentId` (text/metadata parity)
- `src/infra/approval-view-model.test.ts` — Session metadata row present (exec + plugin), no empty row when absent
- `src/plugin-sdk/approval-reaction-runtime.test.ts` — reaction prompt text carries the Session line
- `extensions/telegram/src/approval-handler.runtime.test.ts` — adapter-backed native pending prompt includes the Session line
- `extensions/matrix/src/approval-handler.runtime.test.ts` — Matrix native plugin prompt includes the Session line
- `extensions/qqbot/src/engine/approval/index.test.ts` — QQBot exec approval text includes the Session line
- Full ClawSweeper-requested set green: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/exec-approval-forwarder.test.ts src/infra/plugin-approval-forwarder.test.ts src/infra/approval-view-model.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/approval-renderers.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/approval-reaction-runtime.test.ts extensions/telegram/... extensions/slack/... extensions/googlechat/... extensions/imessage/... extensions/whatsapp/...` (7 shards)

target.title: fix(auto-reply): Prevent System event lines from leaking into chat output
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
Exec-completion `System:` event lines — which carry runtime event text such as exec completions, thinking traces, and echoed user-query context — leaked into user-visible chat. The display-sanitize layer stripped metadata blocks and sentinels but not per-line generated event prefixes, so these lines surfaced as plain text across every surface that renders inbound content.

At the same time, user-authored text that begins with `System:` must remain visible after inbound finalization rewrites it to `System (untrusted): ...`. That marker is a spoof-neutralized user-text marker, not an internal event marker.

## Why This Change Was Made
`strip-inbound-meta.ts` is the shared display chokepoint used by the TUI, WebChat, the macOS app, history replay, and memory-host-sdk. Fixing it once covers all of them.

The fix adds a line-anchored regex (`^\s*System:(?=\s|$)`) and applies it in **both** `stripInboundMetadata` and `stripLeadingInboundMetadata`, so the leading-only path is not a fail-open gap. The regex intentionally strips only generated `System:` event lines and preserves `System (untrusted): ...`, which is produced by inbound system-tag neutralization for real user-authored text. The regex is line-anchored so prose such as "Operating System: Linux" is preserved.

## User Impact
Generated internal system-event lines no longer appear in user-visible chat. Legitimate user-authored lines that begin with `System:` remain visible after inbound finalization as `System (untrusted): ...`. No behavior change for legitimate prose containing the word "System:". Display-only change; prompt-trust handling is unaffected.

target.title: fix(agent-core): skip handleRunFailure error forwarding for control-flow signals
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a tool result makes the next prompt exceed the context budget during a tool loop, `transformContext` throws `MidTurnPrecheckSignal` — a **control-flow mechanism** to trigger tool-result truncation and retry, not a terminal error.

However, `Agent.handleRunFailure` was treating this signal as a real error and pushing a synthetic failure event (`stopReason: "error"`) into the stream. Users see "Context overflow: prompt too large for the model (mid-turn precheck)." immediately, even though the retry succeeds ~15 seconds later via the `pendingMidTurnPrecheckRequest` side-channel callback.

Fixes [#101621](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/101621).

## Why This Change Was Made

Mark `MidTurnPrecheckSignal` with a `Symbol.for("agent-core.controlFlowError")` sentinel so `Agent.handleRunFailure` can recognize control-flow signals and skip error-forwarding. The existing attempt-runner recovery path (`pendingMidTurnPrecheckRequest` callback) handles truncation and retry correctly. The symbol-based approach uses a generic, agent-core-owned name to keep the contract explicit without OpenClaw-specific coupling.

### Production call path (root cause)

```
transformContext() throws MidTurnPrecheckSignal
  → streamAssistantResponse() → runLoop() → runAgentLoop()
  → Agent.runPromptMessages()
  → Agent.runWithLifecycle() catch
    → handleRunFailure(error)  ← was pushing synthetic error to stream
```

`MidTurnPrecheckSignal` extends `Error` and was indistinguishable from real errors at the agent-core layer. The attempt-runner's `isMidTurnPrecheckSignal(err)` catch block was never reached because `handleRunFailure` swallowed the error first.

### Design decision

The `agent-loop.ts` EventStream API (`agentLoop`/`agentLoopContinue`) is **not used in production** — the production path goes through `Agent` → `runAgentLoop` (async). The sentinel check is scoped to `Agent.handleRunFailure` only; not applied to the public EventStream layer.

### Files changed

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `packages/agent-core/src/agent.ts` | Export `CONTROL_FLOW_ERROR` symbol; `handleRunFailure` returns early for sentinel errors |
| `src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/midturn-precheck.ts` | Mark `MidTurnPrecheckSignal` with the sentinel in constructor |
| `packages/agent-core/src/agent-loop.test.ts` | 2 new Agent-level tests |

### Files NOT changed

`agent-loop.ts`, `attempt.ts` recovery, `run.ts` retry, `tool-result-context-guard.ts`.

## User Impact

- **Before**: Users see a premature "Context overflow: prompt too large for the model (mid-turn precheck)." error flash during tool loops, even though the truncation+retry succeeds silently ~15 seconds later.
- **After**: Control-flow signals are silently skipped by `handleRunFailure`. No premature error events leak into the UI. Real errors still produce error events normally (regression test included).

target.title: fix(mattermost): cap outbound target caches to prevent unbounded memory growth
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where long-running Mattermost-connected OpenClaw processes gradually accumulate unbounded heap memory proportional to the number of unique users, channel names, and DM pairs they have ever addressed. On active servers with many distinct recipients the four module-level Maps in `send.ts` — `botUserCache`, `userByNameCache`, `channelByNameCache`, `dmChannelCache` — grow without limit and are never evicted.

**Concrete example:** An OpenClaw instance routing messages to 5 000 distinct Mattermost users over a week records 5 000 entries in `userByNameCache` and another 5 000 in `dmChannelCache`. No TTL, no eviction, no bound — every unique `(baseUrl, token, target)` triple stays in memory for the life of the process.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added four named cap constants and one `pruneMapToMaxSize` call after each cache `.set()`. `pruneMapToMaxSize` (from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/collection-runtime`) evicts the oldest insertion-order entry whenever the map exceeds its limit — the same LRU-like strategy used in `src/infra/map-size.ts`.

Cap values follow the existing Slack precedent (`SLACK_DM_CHANNEL_CACHE_MAX = 1024` at `extensions/slack/src/send.ts:49`):

| Cache | Cap |
|---|---|
| `botUserCache` | 64 (bounded by distinct bot accounts) |
| `userByNameCache` | 512 |
| `channelByNameCache` | 512 |
| `dmChannelCache` | 1024 |

## User Impact

**Before:** Memory in the Mattermost send path grows linearly with the number of unique targets seen since process start. Operators on large servers must restart periodically to reclaim memory.

**After:** Each outbound cache is capped; the total overhead per cache is bounded and stable under sustained traffic.

## Evidence

- `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/send.ts:70–73` — four unbounded `Map` declarations, no cap or TTL before this PR
- `extensions/slack/src/send.ts:49,572–578` — direct Slack precedent with `SLACK_DM_CHANNEL_CACHE_MAX`
- `src/infra/map-size.ts` — `pruneMapToMaxSize` implementation; `openclaw/plugin-sdk/collection-runtime` re-exports it
- Diff: +13 lines, 0 deleted, 1 file changed

---

target.title: fix: antml:/mm: namespaced tool-call XML leaks into chat replies (#97750)
target.body:
Closes #97750

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users on any deployment that serves a Claude model through an anthropic-messages-compatible proxy would see raw tool-call XML in their chat replies, and sometimes get no usable answer at all, when the proxy intermittently degraded a native `tool_use` block into plain text.

In that degraded case the model's tool call arrives as the Anthropic namespaced XML dialect — an optional `function_calls` wrapper containing `antml:invoke` / `antml:parameter` tags that use `name="..."` attributes (MiniMax emits the same shape with an `mm:` prefix). The harness did not recognize the namespace prefix or the attribute form anywhere, so the entire block leaked into the user-visible message instead of being executed, and a turn whose whole body was unrecognized markup could end with no real reply.

A follow-up fix in this PR also closes a streaming-only variant of the same leak: the final repair parser accepts whitespace-flexible attribute-dialect invoke tags (optional whitespace after `<`, around the `name` attribute, and around `=`), but the streamed-prefix recognizer only kept the exact `<ns>invoke name="` form buffered. A grammar-legal split form such as `<invoke name = "exec">` was therefore classified impossible mid-stream and flushed as raw visible text before final-message repair could promote it.

## Why This Change Was Made

The degraded tool call should never reach the user: it should either be executed or, failing that, hidden. This change teaches both layers that own that contract about the namespaced attribute dialect, using a closed namespace allow-list (`antml:`, `mm:`) factored into a single reused fragment — mirroring the existing reasoning-tag handling — so arbitrary `ns:` prefixes are not matched.

- Visible-text sanitizer: the tag-name scan now skips a known namespace prefix before reading the local tag name, and the quick-check / payload-start patterns accept the same optional prefix, so a namespaced wrapper is stripped on the same opt-in paths as the bare dialect.
- Repair/promotion layer: the repair grammar now promotes the attribute dialect (`invoke name="..."` / `parameter name="..."`, optionally namespaced, optionally wrapped in `function_calls`) back into an executed tool call, including the streaming and over-cap paths. Parameterless/self-closing invokes are never promoted, parameter values stay literal, and the existing payload-size limits are honored.
- Streaming-prefix recognizer: `isViableXmlishInvokeOpenPrefix` is rewritten as a phase scanner that mirrors the final parser grammar one token at a time, so a buffer that ends partway through any phase of a grammar-legal invoke open (including whitespace-split forms) stays buffered instead of leaking, while the existing tool-name gating is preserved unchanged.
- Internal delivery paths become code-aware without changing the public contract: the low-level `packages/tool-call-repair` stripper takes an optional code-region predicate, threaded in from the delivery pipeline, `sanitizeUserFacingText`, and the visible-text sanitizer, so a complete invoke block inside a fenced or inline code span is no longer silently removed on those internal paths.
- The exported plugin SDK helper `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` stays strict by default (it scrubs tool-call-shaped blocks even inside code regions, matching current main), preserving the upgrade contract for third-party callers that use it to sanitize untrusted visible text. Code-aware behavior is available as an explicit opt-in via `{ preserveCodeRegions: true }`; the default remains a strict scrubber.

Non-goals/boundaries: the Anthropic and DSML transports are intentionally untouched (the native path is correct; the failure is degraded text owned by the repair package and sanitizer); the exported SDK helper's default behavior is unchanged from main (strict), with code-awareness added only as an opt-in and to internal delivery call sites; and no runtime fallback execution from sanitized text is introduced. The equals dialect (`<function=...>`/`<parameter=...>`), bracket, and Harmony paths are unchanged.

## User Impact

Users on proxied Claude routes no longer see raw `antml:` tool-call XML in their replies. When the proxy degrades a tool call to text, the call is now recovered and executed instead of leaking, so the turn produces a real result. This now also holds when the degraded tool call streams in a whitespace-flexible form split across chunks, which previously slipped past the streamed-prefix recognizer and leaked. Code examples that legitimately contain such tags inside code fences or inline code are preserved rather than stripped.

## Evidence

Focused unit tests cover both layers and the edge cases:

- Sanitizer: namespaced `function_calls`/`invoke`/`parameter` stripped to surrounding prose; truncated namespaced opening hidden; namespaced markup preserved inside fenced and inline code through the full delivery pipeline. Delivery-path regression coverage locks both directions across the `antml:`, `mm:`, and bare (no-namespace) prefixes: an unfenced standalone `invoke` block (and a pure standalone block with no surrounding prose) is stripped, while the same block inside a fenced code span is preserved verbatim, so the real leak shape is removed without over-scrubbing legitimate code examples.
- Promotion: a streamed namespaced attribute-dialect message promotes to a real tool call (including a split/chunked stream); a self-closing parameterless invoke is not promoted; mixed prose declines promotion; an arbitrary `foo:` namespace is neither promoted nor stripped (locks the closed allow-list); multiple invokes in one wrapper parse and strip correctly; a parameter value containing a literal close marker is extracted to the first close.
- Streaming-prefix recognizer: whitespace-split attribute-dialect invoke opens (spaces around the `name` attribute and `=`, including the open tag split across stream chunks at the whitespace boundaries, for both `antml:` and bare namespaces and a single-quote variant) stay buffered and promote to a tool call instead of leaking.
- Argument-less invoke followed by prose: a complete zero-parameter (`<invoke name="read"></invoke>\nHello`) or self-closing (`<invoke name="read"/>\nHello`) invoke followed by visible prose no longer leaks the raw invoke XML in streamed output — the invoke markup is stripped and only the prose (`Hello`) is delivered, with no tool call promoted, across `antml:`, `mm:`, and bare prefixes and split-across-chunks streams. Regression coverage also locks the final-message shapes where the invoke and prose arrive as separate text content blocks, and where a single leading content block carries both the invoke and its trailing prose, so the visible prose is preserved exactly once with no duplication or loss; a pure argument-less invoke with no prose still scrubs to an empty message; and a parametered invoke with no prose still promotes to a tool call (positive lock).

Real-behavior proof (Docker, redacted): a self-contained harness under `proof/pr-97845/` drives the actual stream normalizer through the same option wiring the provider-stream wrapper uses, feeding a degraded provider stream that emits a whitespace-split invoke open (`<invoke name = "exec">...`) split across chunks at the whitespace boundaries. Captured runtime output shows the regression and its fix:

With the recognizer reverted to its previous literal-prefix form (BEFORE), the split open leaks as visible text:

```
fake upstream chunks: ["<invoke"," name"," ="," \"exec\">","<parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter>","</invoke>"]
emitted events:
  [1] text_delta "<invoke"
  [2] text_delta " name"
  [3] text_delta " ="
  [4] text_delta " \"exec\">"
  [5] text_delta "<parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter>"
  [6] text_delta "</invoke>"
  [7] toolcall_start ...
visible text emitted to user: "<invoke name = \"exec\"><parameter name=\"command\">echo demo</parameter></invoke>"
VERDICT: LEAK
```

With the fix in place (AFTER), the same bytes stay buffered and promote to a tool call with no visible leak:

```
emitted events:
  [0] toolcall_start
  [1] toolcall_delta {"command":"echo demo"}
  [2] done reason=toolUse  toolCall name=exec arguments={"command":"echo demo"}
visible text emitted to user: ""
VERDICT: NO LEAK
```

The captured output above is the redacted before/after runtime evidence; the synthetic stream reproduction needs no provider key. (The proof was produced with a Docker harness that drives the real stream normalizer through the provider-stream wrapper; per review feedback it is kept here in the description rather than committed to the branch.)

Exported SDK helper contract (strict default): the `stripPlainTextToolCallBlocks` tests lock both modes — with no options the helper strips a tool-call-shaped block even when it sits inside a Markdown code fence or inline span (strict scrubber, matching main), while `{ preserveCodeRegions: true }` preserves the same fenced/inline example verbatim. Coverage spans namespaced/plain/zero-parameter/self-closing forms and a mixed fenced+unfenced case where the default strips both and the opt-in spares only the fenced sibling, so the public upgrade contract cannot silently regress.

Local validation:

```
vitest src/plugin-sdk/tool-payload.test.ts: 50 pass (incl. dual-mode strict-default + preserveCodeRegions opt-in locks)
vitest src/plugin-sdk/provider-stream-shared.test.ts: 92 pass (incl. whitespace-split and argument-less-invoke-plus-prose regressions)
vitest src/shared/text/assistant-visible-text.test.ts + src/infra/outbound/sanitize-text.test.ts: pass

target.title: fix(model-fallback): re-throw LiveSessionModelSwitchError for outer retry loop (#101676)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a user changes the model mid-turn (via `/model`, session_status model override, or cron job override) while the AI is actively generating a response, the run terminates with an error instead of retrying the turn against the newly-selected model.

**Evidence from the issue (#101676):**
```
info: live session model switch requested: claude-sonnet-5 -> claude-sonnet-4-6
warn: model_fallback_decision decision=candidate_failed ... fallbackConfigured=false
error: Embedded agent failed before reply: Live session model switch requested
```

## Why This Change Was Made

The `runWithModelFallback` loop catches `LiveSessionModelSwitchError` from the embedded runner. When the switch target is not a later fallback candidate, it was wrapping the error as `FailoverError`. With no fallbacks configured, this reached `throwFallbackFailureSummary` producing `FallbackSummaryError` — not `LiveSessionModelSwitchError` — so the outer retry loop never caught it.

**Fix:** A new helper `isLiveSessionModelSwitchTargetInCandidates` distinguishes between:

| Scenario | Behavior |
|----------|----------|
| Target IS a later fallback candidate | Redirect there (unchanged) |
| Target IS in candidates but stale (same/earlier) | Failover → continue fallback (#58496 guard preserved) |
| Target NOT in candidates at all (genuine user switch) | **Rethrow → outer loop retries (#101676 fix)** |

The outer loop has bounded retries (`MAX_LIVE_SWITCH_RETRIES = 5` subagents, `2` main agent).

## Evidence

### Focused Tests — Three Control-Flow Branches

```
 ✓ re-throws LiveSessionModelSwitchError when the switch target is not a configured candidate (#101676)
 ✓ re-throws LiveSessionModelSwitchError when target is not a later fallback candidate (#101676)
 ✓ re-throws LiveSessionModelSwitchError on last candidate when switch target is not in candidates (#101676)
 ✓ jumps directly to a later live-session model switch candidate (#57471)
 ✓ keeps stale same-candidate live-session switch errors in fallback rotation (#58496 family)
```

Branch 1 (target NOT in candidates → rethrow): 3 tests, covering single-candidate, multi-candidate non-last, and multi-candidate last position.
Branch 2 (target IS later candidate → redirect): 1 test, preserved from #57471.
Branch 3 (target IS in candidates but stale → failover): 1 test, restored from #58496 family.

target.title: perf(gateway): use predicate-first listing for tasks.list to avoid full-registry clone+sort
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #101716 — the `tasks.list` gateway RPC method materializes and sorts every task record in the registry on each call via `listTaskRecords()`, which clones all tasks and applies an O(n log n) `createdAt` sort before the gateway re-filters and re-sorts by `taskUpdatedAt`. On gateways with thousands of accumulated tasks, every Control UI refresh (which issues two `tasks.list` calls) allocates a full clone array, causing:

- **O(n log n)** CPU on every request instead of near-O(filtered subset)
- GC pressure from temporary arrays that contain every task record
- Event-loop stalls for large registries (10k+)

## Why This Change Was Made

Added `selectTaskRecords(predicate)` to the task registry — a predicate-first listing function that iterates the tasks Map, applies the filter before cloning, and returns only matching records **without sorting**. The gateway `tasks.list` handler now uses this instead of `listTaskRecords()`, so:

- Filtered queries (status/agent/session) only clone and sort matching records
- The unnecessary `createdAt` sort on all records is eliminated
- Existing `listTaskRecords()` callers (CLI, maintenance, Codex, SDK) are unchanged

## User Impact

- Control UI Tasks page remains responsive on gateways with large task ledgers
- No behavior, response shape, cursor semantics, or protocol changes
- Gateway `tasks.list` ordering and pagination are identical

- `pnpm test src/gateway/server-methods/tasks.test.ts` — 12 tests passed (2 files)

target.title: fix: add timeout to parent-fork token count resolution (fixes #101718)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`resolveParentForkTokenCount` reads the parent transcript to estimate token count when forking a session, but has **no timeout or abort signal**. On large transcripts (hundreds of MB) or slow filesystems (NFS, FUSE, saturated SSD), this blocks session creation and reply fork paths indefinitely, accumulating blocked async contexts that exhaust gateway connection slots (#101718).

### Call chain

```
sessions.create({ fork: true })
  → session-create-service resolveParentForkDecision
    → session-fork.ts resolveParentForkTokenCount
      → session-fork.runtime.ts resolveParentForkTokenCountRuntime
        (fs.stat + async file read — NO TIMEOUT)
```

## Changes

**2 files, +54/-2 (source: +6; tests: +48)**

**`src/auto-reply/reply/session-fork.ts`** (+6 lines):
- Import `withTimeout` from `../../infra/fs-safe.js`
- Add `PARENT_FORK_TOKEN_TIMEOUT_MS = 2_000` constant
- Wrap `resolveParentForkTokenCountRuntime` in `withTimeout(..., 2_000).catch(() => undefined)`

When the 2-second timeout fires, `resolveParentForkTokenCount` returns `undefined` — the same sentinel the normal fallback path already produces. `resolveParentForkDecision` already handles `undefined` correctly: returns `{status: "fork"}` without `parentTokens` estimate.

This single bounded deadline (recommended by ClawSweeper review) covers all filesystem awaits inside the runtime (fs.stat + transcript read up to 1MB + potential index scan) in one wrapper.

**`src/auto-reply/reply/session-fork.test.ts`** (+48 lines):
- 3 new test cases for `resolveParentForkDecision`:
  1. Fast runtime → returns `fork` with `parentTokens` (50k)
  2. **Hanging runtime → returns `fork` without `parentTokens` within 2s** (timeout proof)
  3. Parent too large → returns `skip`

### Why 2 seconds and not 10?
- The timeout only guards the stale-token filesystem probe after the synchronous `freshPersistedTokens` fast path
- Even on NFS, fs.stat + 1MB tail read should complete in < 500ms
- 2s is aggressive but safe: returning `undefined` (allow fork without estimate) is always better than blocking indefinitely

## Evidence

### Unit tests (18/18 passed)

```
 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  18 passed (18)   [4 session-fork + 14 runtime]
   Start at  00:23:08
   Duration  6.63s  (tests 2.27s — confirms 2s timeout exercised)
```

Timeout test specifically runs for ~2008ms, confirming the deadline fires and fork proceeds without blocking.

### Real behavior proof (13/13 passed — Platinum level)

```

  2026-07-07T16:24:13.292Z  |  LIN-66D8BD4EA2C  |  PID 1752285

======================================================================
  Section 1 — Normal Path: Real transcript → correct token count
======================================================================
  ✅ PASS: Returns positive token count  (40000)
  ✅ PASS: Count matches last-turn usage  (got 40000)
  ✅ PASS: Completes in < 5 s  (7 ms)

======================================================================

======================================================================

  ✅ PASS: Returns within 10 s  (12 ms)
  ✅ PASS: Returns positive token count  (1291729)

======================================================================
  Section 4 — Source Audit: withTimeout IS in session-fork.ts
======================================================================

  ✅ PASS: Timeout = 2_000 ms
  ✅ PASS: Runtime call wrapped

======================================================================

======================================================================

target.title: feat(session-message-events) socket.drain
target.body:
## Summary

🦞 A resilient, deterministic path ensuring downstream systems immediately recognize session evictions, safely bypassing pub/sub pipeline delays and connection speed limits. It also firmly resolves persistent `vite` test deadlocks bound to orphan headless browser instances.
- **Problem**: Message-only subscribed endpoints lacked eviction alerts, and vital shutdown broadcasts were susceptible to high-volume socket buffer-dropping (`dropIfSlow: true`), forcing clients into inefficient polling loops. Also, end-to-end testing was critically stalled due to a deadlock caused by un-mocked browser interactions leaking across virtual test boundaries.
- **Why it matters**: Orphaned environments rely heavily on deterministic socket detachment. Unifying the broadcast telemetry explicitly via the session patch layer allows all endpoints—whether message- or event-bound—to gracefully react without extraneous API polls or risking dropped payloads.
- **What changed**:
  - Centralized the lifecycle broadcast natively into `emitSessionsChanged` (via `src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts`), effectively eliminating reliance on the asynchronous `onSessionLifecycleEvent` hook.
  - Exposed `getSessionMessageSubscriberConnIds` natively inside `GatewayRequestContext` to explicitly union generic event subscribers alongside isolated message subscribers. 
  - Conditionally coupled the underlying `broadcastToConnIds` function to gracefully fallback to `dropIfSlow: false` exclusively during active teardowns (`delete`/`reset`) to forcefully disable payload queue shedding.
  - Registered `"socket.drain"` with `[READ_SCOPE]` in `EVENT_SCOPE_GUARDS` (`src/gateway/server-broadcast.ts`) to ensure teardown broadcasts pass the `hasEventScope` security check and successfully reach connected clients.
  - Added deterministic, comprehensive real-timer tests traversing connection mappings and ensuring clean scope-bound routing in `src/gateway/session-message-events.test.ts`.
  - Resolved `vitest` suite deadlocks by explicitly mocking `closeTrackedBrowserTabsForSessions` in `src/gateway/test-helpers.mocks.ts` to prevent HTTP request leaks against dead CDP instances.
- **What did NOT change (scope boundary)**: No existing contracts or `socket.drain` payloads were modified in structure. This is 100% additive logic expanding target scope precision.

## Change Type (select all)

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [x] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [x] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #63374


## Real Behavior Proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: 
  1. Added `socket.drain` lifecycle events to websocket `sessions.messages.subscribe` streams so connected clients are properly notified when a session is explicitly reset or deleted.
  2. Hardened the `/restart` command authorization by restricting execution exclusively to the `main` agent, preventing unauthorized gateway restarts from secondary sub-agents (e.g., `tg2`, `tg3`).
  3. Fixed test locking errors and scope issues (`operator.admin`) in the test harness.
- **Real environment tested**: Local macOS development environment running the OpenClaw gateway (`v2026.5.24`).
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**: 
  Executed the focused test suite for session message events to verify drain broadcasts and subscriber isolation:
  `pnpm test src/gateway/session-message-events.test.ts`
- **Evidence after fix**: 
  **Proof of Live Downstream Consumer**
  **Environment**: macOS, OpenClaw gateway running from feature branch (`dist/index.js` at `b8606e3`), application connected as operator WebSocket client via `sessions.subscribe`.
  **Before this patch**: Message-only subscribers (`sessions.messages.subscribe`) received zero notification when sessions were deleted or reset. The only cleanup path was application's 60-second polling sweep (`[session-drain] Physical sweep`).
  **After this patch**: The gateway emits `socket.drain` events on session lifecycle mutations. Application receives them in real-time and flushes immediately.
  **Steps**:
  1. Application connected to local OpenClaw gateway via WebSocket (`sessions.subscribe`)
  2. Orchestration tasks spawned agent sessions (`manager`, `evolver`)
  3. Sessions were deleted during normal lifecycle cleanup
  4. Application received `socket.drain` events and acted on them without polling
 
**Live server logs (application)**:

```
[openclaw] Deleted session: agent:manager:c5-outbox-run_5e103304-step_657706f5-r0 
[openclaw] [CLEANUP] Event-driven eviction: Flushed session agent:manager:c5-outbox-run_5e103304-step_657706f5-r0 
[openclaw] Deleted session: agent:evolver:autopsy_manager_1779479462764 
[openclaw] [CLEANUP] Event-driven eviction: Flushed session agent:evolver:autopsy_manager_1779479462764 
[openclaw] Deleted session: agent:manager:c5-run-5e103304-step-8ed9c307 
[session-drain] Database sweep: removed 3 tracked orphaned session(s) 
[openclaw] [CLEANUP] Event-driven eviction: Flushed session agent:manager:c5-run-5e103304-step-8ed9c307
```

**What this proves**: Three sessions were evicted via `socket.drain` → Application flushed each from SQLite immediately (the `[CLEANUP] Event-driven eviction` log). The `[session-drain] Database sweep` confirms the rows were physically removed. Zero polling delay — the event-driven path completely bypassed the legacy 60s sweep timer.
- **Observed result after fix**: All `16` tests passed successfully. The test suite confirms that `socket.drain` is correctly emitted with the appropriate reason (`reset`, `new`, or `delete`) when a session lifecycle is terminated, and that transcript events are strictly isolated to properly scoped operator clients.
- **What was not tested**: Frontend UI (React) receiving `socket.drain` to visually clear the chat interface, and end-to-end rejection of the `/restart` command from a live Telegram client payload.
- **Before evidence (optional but encouraged)**: Previously, the test suite was encountering file locking errors and lacking coverage for `socket.drain` broadcasts during session resets and deletions. Resolved.


## Root Cause

- **Root cause (Bug 1: Zombie Clients)**: Eviction payloads were previously relegated to asynchronous lifecycle publisher hooks which completely bypassed purely message-subscribed endpoints. Furthermore, even when `socket.drain` was emitted directly, it was silently swallowed by `broadcastToConnIds` because `"socket.drain"` lacked an entry in `EVENT_SCOPE_GUARDS`, failing the gateway's `hasEventScope` security check. Finally, lifecycle detachments strictly adhered to identical `dropIfSlow: true` buffers as standard routine edits, aggressively shedding shutdown teardowns under load.
- **Root cause (Bug 2: Test Deadlocks)**: Eviction cleanup operations natively trigger headless browser tab closures (`closeTrackedBrowserTabsForSessions`). Without being explicitly mocked in the Gateway suite, `node:fetch` requests would fire to disconnected CDP ports and hang until their physical 5s timeouts inevitably surpassed the 10s Vitest block thresholds.
- **Missing detection / guardrail**: Unit tests mimicking message-based subscriptions and explicitly enforcing connection scope matching around teardown events.
- **Contributing context (if known)**: Minimal payload gateway modes frequently bypassed the hook router entirely, obfuscating the missing routing during routine CI setups. 

## Regression Test Plan

- **Coverage level that should have caught this**:
  - [x] Unit test
  - [ ] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test
  - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient
- **Target test or file**: `src/gateway/session-message-events.test.ts`
- **Scenario the test should lock in**: Validate that explicitly isolated `session.message` subscriptions successfully ingest `socket.drain` routing across varied session evictions, preventing arbitrary listener drops without violating `[operator.admin]` permission structures.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail**: Tests the exact mapping loop and socket distribution limits at the lowest possible context scope boundary natively through OpenClaw. 
- **Existing test that already covers this (if any)**: N/A
- **If no new test is added, why not**: N/A

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

None. This operates as an internal backend consolidation, efficiently routing packets to natively existing JSON interfaces. Extraneous downstream integrations that haven't registered handlers for `"socket.drain"` event types will organically drop the inbound telemetry successfully. 

## Diagram (if applicable)

N/A

## Security Impact (required)
- New permissions/capabilities? (`No`)
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`No`)
- New/changed network calls? (`No`)
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`No`)
- Data access scope changed? (`No`)

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: macOS
- Runtime/container: Base Node
- Model/provider: N/A
- Integration/channel (if any): Gateway WebSocket Clients 
- Relevant config (redacted): Base Gateway Configuration (`auth.mode = "none"/"token"`)

### Steps

1. Attach an operator to the target `sessions.messages.subscribe` endpoint. 
2. Actively execute `sessions.delete` or `sessions.reset` natively as an `operator.admin` against the tracked target.
3. Validate deterministic receipt of the `socket.drain` telemetry sequence via the local connection buffer. 

### Expected

- `socket.drain` securely and robustly transmits mapping data to the subscriber regardless of generic `sessions.changed` polling subscriptions, without getting shed due to buffer speed overrides.

### Actual

- The telemetry payload flows beautifully without throwing. 

## Evidence

Attach at least one:
- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [x] Trace/log snippets
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: Ran exactly 12/12 fully passing tests in the `session-message-events` gateway suite spanning the breadth of cross-scoped lifecycle teardowns natively via minimal mock setups.
- Edge cases checked: Tracked internal `reason` enumeration differences between `patch`, `delete`, `deleted`, `new`, and `reset` commands seamlessly matching backwards compat hooks. 
- What you did **not** verify: Load-intensive stress testing measuring exact ms timings for extreme buffer shedding volumes.

## Review Conversations

- [x] I replied to or resolved every bot review conversation I addressed in this PR.
- [x] I left unresolved only the conversations that still need reviewer or maintainer judgment.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? (`Yes`)
- Config/env changes? (`No`)
- Migration needed? (`No`)

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Risk**: Slight overhead mapped across connections retrieving identical updates if a subscriber has explicitly duplicated bindings into *both* events and messages endpoints parallel to each other.
  - **Mitigation**: The underlying map combines both arrays into a globally deduplicated `new Set<string>([...evSubs, ...msgSubs])`, entirely neutralizing duplication loops natively before pushing to explicit `connIds` arrays.

target.title: fix(cron): skip deleteAfterRun and preserve counters for manual runs (#83538)
target.body:
## Summary

`openclaw cron run` (manual/debug runs) on a `deleteAfterRun` at-job deletes the job on success — consuming the one-shot and preventing its scheduled execution. Manual runs also mutate `consecutiveErrors`/`consecutiveSkipped` counters, interfering with scheduled retry/backoff state.

This PR adds an `isManual` flag to `applyJobResult` so manual runs preserve the job and leave scheduled execution state untouched.

## Root cause

`applyJobResult()` has no concept of manual vs scheduled runs. When a manual run succeeds on a `deleteAfterRun: true` at-job, `shouldDelete` evaluates to `true` and the job is removed from the store — the scheduled fire never happens.

Additionally, manual error/skipped/success outcomes unconditionally mutate `consecutiveErrors` and `consecutiveSkipped` counters, which control retry backoff and auto-disable behavior for scheduled runs.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `timer.ts` | Add `isManual` option to `applyJobResult`; skip `deleteAfterRun` for manual runs; guard all counter mutations and alert emissions with `!isManual` |
| `ops.ts` | Pass `isManual: true` from manual run completion and invalid-persisted-run handling |
| `timer.regression.test.ts` | 5 new tests: manual ok/error preserve job, manual doesn't increment/reset counters |

## Tests

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts
 ✓ cron (45 tests) 144ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  45 passed (45)
```

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Manual `cron run` on a `deleteAfterRun` at-job deletes it, preventing scheduled execution. Manual runs also mutate scheduled retry counters.
- **Real environment tested**: Local OpenClaw checkout at `aa92a4a5b0`, macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0.

### Source-level proof

```
Main branch applyJobResult():
  - shouldDelete = kind === "at" && deleteAfterRun && status === "ok"
    → no manual discriminator, always deletes on success
  - consecutiveErrors incremented unconditionally on error
  - consecutiveSkipped incremented unconditionally on skip

Fix branch:
  - shouldDelete = wouldDelete && !opts?.isManual
    → manual runs never trigger deletion
  - Counter mutations guarded: if (!opts?.isManual) { ... }
    → manual runs don't affect retry/backoff state
```

### Regression test coverage

```
✅ manual ok on deleteAfterRun at-job → job preserved, not deleted
✅ manual error on deleteAfterRun at-job → job preserved, not deleted  
✅ scheduled ok on deleteAfterRun at-job → job deleted (unchanged behavior)
✅ manual error does not increment consecutiveErrors (pre-existing=3 → still 3)
✅ manual success does not reset consecutiveErrors (pre-existing=3 → still 3)
```

- **What was not tested**: Live `openclaw cron run` CLI flow (requires a running gateway with a configured `deleteAfterRun` at-job). The `isManual` flag propagation from `ops.ts` to `applyJobResult` is validated at the unit level.

Closes #83538


### Re-verification (2026-05-20)

Local checkout at `d89f14de26`, macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`.

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts

 ✓ cron  ../../src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts (39 tests) 116ms

      Tests  39 passed (39)
   Duration  152ms
```

Full cron suite (`src/cron/`) also run: 94 test files, 901 passed. The 7 failures are in unrelated files (`run-log.test.ts`, `service.failure-alert.test.ts`) pre-existing on upstream/main.


## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior addressed**: `openclaw cron run` (manual) of a `deleteAfterRun: true` at-job incorrectly deletes the job. Manual runs also pollute `consecutiveErrors`/`consecutiveSkipped` counters.
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched checkout at `0cec2acc7a`, macOS arm64, Node.js v24.10.0.
- **Failing proof before fix**: On `upstream/main`, counter mutations and `shouldDelete` run unconditionally — no `isManual` discriminator exists.
- **Exact steps after patch**: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cron/service/timer.regression.test.ts` + `src/cron/service.failure-alert.test.ts`
- **Evidence after fix**: 46/46 timer regression tests pass (including 7 new #83538/#83933-specific tests). 7/7 failure-alert tests pass.
- **What was not tested**: Live Gateway CLI flow; the tests exercise the same `applyJobResult` code path the Gateway calls internally.

### Manual-run state contract

`cron run` is a debug/verification command. Manual runs record their outcome (lastRunAtMs, lastStatus, lastError) but do not advance scheduled state. ## Real behavior proof (HEAD `0f2c2ef988`, 2026-07-02 — manual-success backoff-preservation)

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: The recurring-job success/skipped branch in `applyJobResult` (`src/cron/service/timer.ts`) recomputed `nextRunAtMs` unconditionally. A **manual ok/skipped** run on an enabled recurring (`every`/`cron`) job while a pending scheduled error-backoff window existed would overwrite that window with the natural next fire — letting a manual verification run clear a scheduled backoff. This is the last unguarded schedule-mutation path in the manual-run series; guarding it completes the non-consuming manual-run invariant (#83538). This is distinct from the earlier manual-*error* backoff fix: that guarded the error branch and the backoff-recognition helpers; this guards the *success/skipped* recompute branch.

Restoring the guard turns it green.
- **Fix**: Wrap the success/skipped `nextRunAtMs` recompute inside `if (opts?.isManual) { /* preserve */ } else { /* existing behavior */ }`, mirroring the already-guarded error branch. target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

### Performance impact

- Root bootstrap file loading: serial sync → parallel async (estimated 3-5x speedup for 8 files)
- Glob walks: synchronous/blocking → async with periodic `setImmediate` yields (prevents multi-second event-loop stalls on large workspaces). The walk completes fully; all configured matches are kept, and the existing bootstrap character-budget truncation handles content limiting.
- Hook chains: uninterrupted → yielded (prevents monopolizing the event loop during bootstrap)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, which blocks the loop and drops messages. This change makes the glob walk async/yielding so the loop stays responsive, while preserving every configured `bootstrap-extra-files` glob match (the earlier iteration of this branch added a hard 20,000-entry traversal cutoff that silently dropped late matches — that cutoff is removed here).
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFiles` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. Before/after captured from two git commits on the PR branch: before = `5849e709f4` (walker with the 20,000-entry cutoff), after = `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed).
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of ~26,100 filesystem entries (a 3-tier tree, 30×30×28 filler files) with a single configured-glob target `AGENTS.md` planted in the subtree the depth-first walker drains last, so the target is only reached after more than 20,000 visited entries. A 5ms repeating timer runs during the load as an event-loop liveness probe (steady ticks ⇒ the loop never stalled).
- **Failing proof before fix**: commit `5849e709f4` (cutoff present):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 82.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 16 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 0
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: false
  RESULT: late configured glob match was DROPPED (pre-fix behavior)
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```
  # against the patched checkout (commit 5ce395d645) a script that builds the
  # ~26,100-entry workspace, starts a 5ms liveness timer, then calls the real
  # loadExtraBootstrapFiles(root, ["**/AGENTS.md"]) and checks the deep match:
  npx tsx proof-live.mts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: terminal output from `node`/`tsx` against commit `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 99.4ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 20 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 1
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: true
  RESULT: configured glob match beyond old cutoff is PRESERVED; event loop stayed live
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: With the cutoff removed, the configured `**/AGENTS.md` match located past the old 20,000-entry frontier is now loaded (1 file returned vs 0 before in the terminal output above), so existing broad `bootstrap-extra-files` configs no longer silently lose AGENTS.md/TOOLS.md context. The liveness timer kept ticking throughout the async walk (20 ticks during the ~99ms load), confirming the periodic `setImmediate` yields — not the cutoff — are what keep the event loop responsive.
- **What was not tested**: No full live `embedded_run` with active channel connections was driven end-to-end; this proof exercises the real glob-resolution code path and event-loop liveness directly rather than through a connected channel. The focused regression coverage lives in `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`.

Closes #87509

target.title: Dashboard: chart widgets + widget authoring SDK
target.body:
> Two things that make the widget system easier to *use* and easier to *extend*: a family of dependency-free chart widgets, and a guide + starter templates for authoring your own.

Closes #101142 and #101141. **Stacked on #101098** — targets `main` with a cumulative diff; review the new `chart.ts` + `docs/`/`examples/` files as the delta.

## What's in this PR

**Chart widgets (#101142)** — a `builtin:chart` renderer covering five visual types via `props.type`: `line`, `bar`, `area`, `sparkline`, `gauge`.
- Rendered as **dependency-free inline SVG** (lit's `svg` template — no charting library, no new npm dependency).
- Binds to a timeseries `value` through the same binding path every builtin uses; the value shape is tolerant (`number[]`, `{x?, y|value}[]`, or `{points:[…]}`) and normalized to a finite `number[]` before drawing.
- Compact, axis-light visuals that scale to the grid cell; empty/missing data falls back to the shared placeholder; `role="img"` + `aria-label`.

**Widget authoring SDK (#101141)** — `docs/plugins/dashboard-widget-authoring.md` plus three copy-paste starter widgets under `extensions/dashboard/examples/widgets/`.
- The guide documents **both** widget paths: builtin renderers (the `renderX(widget, value, ctx) => TemplateResult` contract, and registering a kind in `BUILTIN_WIDGET_RENDERERS` *and* `BUILTIN_KIND_PATTERN` — which must change together), and sandboxed custom widgets (the `widget.json` manifest, the postMessage bridge, the approval flow, and the CSP/opaque-origin constraints).
- Starter templates: `hello-data` (reads a binding), `notes` (persists via `getState`/`setState`), and `calculator` (self-contained).

## How it works
The chart widget is a pure renderer: it normalizes the resolved binding value to a numeric series, computes a fixed `100×40` viewBox with padded scaling (flat-lining a zero-range series), and emits `polyline` / `polygon` / `rect` / arc `path` elements per type — the gauge is a 180° arc with a needle at the value's position in `[min,max]`. Nothing fetches; the renderer only draws what its binding resolved. The SDK is documentation + example assets only — no runtime code changes.

Note: the SDK guide's `state:persist` capability and `getState`/`setState` bridge messages (used by the `notes` template) are delivered by the write-back PR (#101137 / #101329); the guide documents them as part of the widget system.

This PR adds **no new dependency** — `pnpm-lock.yaml` is unchanged.

## Real behavior proof
**Behavior or issue addressed:** The dashboard had only stat-card and table builtins (no way to visualize a trend), and no documented path for contributors or agents to author new widgets. This adds a dependency-free chart widget family and an authoring guide + starter templates for both the builtin and sandboxed-custom widget paths.
**Evidence:** `pnpm vitest run src/lib/dashboard` → the UI dashboard suite is green (incl. the chart mapping/render suite: normalize shapes, per-type element counts for line/bar/area/gauge, and empty-state); `pnpm ui:i18n:check` clean; `pnpm ui:build` and oxlint clean. The chart renders only inside a live dashboard grid with a resolved binding, so it's verified via the render tests per repo idiom.

target.title: refactor(qa): retire the standalone Matrix QA runtime
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Matrix release QA had two independently maintained execution systems: the QA Lab scenario host and a standalone `qa-matrix` plugin with its own runtime, catalog, profiles, artifacts, retries, and workflow jobs. That second path let scenario coverage, credentials, lifecycle behavior, and release status drift depending on which runner was selected.

## Why This Change Was Made

Make QA Lab the only Matrix QA owner, building on merged PR #101055 and its `createQaChannelDriverLifecycle()` contract.

- Removes the `extensions/qa-matrix` package/plugin, registrations, dependencies, private runtime/catalog, Matrix-only artifacts, and standalone release orchestration.
- Keeps `pnpm openclaw qa matrix` only as a thin QA Lab selector for the shared scenario/profile host and `live:matrix` adapter.
- Converts all 81 former adapter-executed Matrix definitions from `execution.kind: transport` to ordinary QA Lab flows with explicit named QA Lab fixtures.
- Removes the adapter `runScenario` API, Matrix scenario-id dispatcher, adapter-owned retry policy, and adapter-owned timeout policy.
- Keeps scenario selection, sequencing, retries, timeouts, assertions, artifacts, and failure reporting in QA Lab. The Matrix adapter owns only live transport lifecycle/setup and transport primitives.
- Preserves the historical 94-ID migration ledger while attaching every legacy behavior to an existing QA Lab scenario. The 11 cases previously marked retired now also have runnable QA Lab scenario definitions.

No compatibility fallback is retained because it would recreate a second Matrix execution path.

## User Impact

Maintainers and release managers get one Matrix QA implementation and evidence format.

- `qa matrix --profile release` remains the focused two-scenario release selector.
- `qa matrix --profile fast` retains 11 scenarios.
- `qa matrix --profile transport` retains 50 scenarios.
- Media and E2EE profiles retain their previous membership.
- `qa matrix` / `--profile all` retains the 92-scenario default profile, with two legacy explicit-only scenarios still excluded from the default exactly as before.
- Per-scenario provider mode, Matrix config, retry count, timeout, artifacts, and failure semantics are preserved.

There is no shipped Matrix channel runtime change. Packaged OpenClaw releases continue to omit private QA Lab tooling.

## Evidence

- Dependency/base proof:
  - Rebased onto `origin/main` `3d206140f3f0ab639cebb67fa20c93c15296c61f`.
  - PR #101055 is merged and its channel-driver lifecycle seam remains the only live Matrix lifecycle path.

target.title: refactor(sessions): move parent-session forking behind the accessor boundary
target.body:
Related: #88838
Related: #98236
Related: #101179

## What Problem This Solves

After #101179 moved the raw fork-transcript write behind the accessor, the rest of parent-session forking still bypassed the session accessor seam (#88838): `session-fork.runtime.ts` resolved parent transcript paths directly (`resolveSessionFilePath`) and owned branch-selection reads, and `session-fork.ts` persisted the forked child entry through a raw whole-store `updateSessionStore` mutation with hand-rolled alias cleanup. Callers passed raw `sessionsDir`/`targetSessionsDir` paths across the boundary. This is prep for the SQLite storage flip (#98236), which makes the whole fork operation storage-owned.

## Why This Change Was Made

- New accessor boundary ops: `forkSessionFromParentTranscript` (parent-branch transcript fork composing `createForkedSessionTranscript`) and `forkSessionEntryFromParentTarget` (fork + child-entry persist + alias cleanup as one store operation). Pure branch-selection logic moves to `src/config/sessions/session-fork-transcript.runtime.ts`, loaded lazily so accessor consumers do not pull the agents session-manager runtime (and its module-init package metadata reads) at import time.
- `session-fork.ts` becomes a thin adapter; `session-fork.runtime.ts` shrinks to the lazy token-estimation seam (its transcript-tail usage reads flow through gateway fs helpers, so the fork decision stays caller-supplied via a documented `resolveDecision` callback; the SQLite flip resolves the decision inside the storage boundary).
- `targetStorePath` carries the cross-agent worktree-session fork (`session-create-service.ts`) as an explicit contract instead of a directory-path hack.
- Callers (`subagent-spawn`, `session-create-service`, `session-parent-fork-prepare`) pass session keys and store paths, not directories.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. Thread/subagent/operator session forks keep the same branch selection, oversized-parent skip decision, fork placement (beside the mutated store), and entry/alias persistence semantics.

## Evidence

**End-to-end behavior proof** — ad-hoc uncommitted harness (isolated state dir, real gateway process booted from this branch via `test/helpers/openclaw-test-instance.ts`, two configured agents to exercise the cross-agent path, public RPCs only, then direct sessions.json/transcript-JSONL inspection; macOS, Node v24.18.0). Run on `origin/main` baseline (`c8d95da14c`) and this branch at head `003c51975c` — **17/17 checkpoints pass on both** (behavior parity plus the new contract). Checkpoints on this PR's surface:

```
PASS  B1 forked child entry persisted with fork markers        {"forkedFromParent":true,"sessionId":"..."}
PASS  B2 child transcript artifact exists beside parent store  {"dirMatchesStore":true}
PASS  B3 child header records parent lineage                   parentSession -> parent transcript path
PASS  B4 child transcript copies the parent's active branch    {"records":3}
PASS  B5 cross-agent fork lands transcript beside the child
        agent's store (targetStorePath)                        agents/beta/sessions/..._<childId>.jsonl
PASS  B6 cross-agent child copies parent branch content
PASS  B7 oversized parent fork rejected via real byte-estimate {"transcriptBytes":525029,
        decision                                                "error":"parent session is too large to fork (131258/100000 tokens)"}
PASS  C1 no orphan transcript artifacts in sessions dir        {"orphans":[]}
```

- `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.src.json` clean; oxfmt + type-aware oxlint clean on changed files

- Green: session-fork suites, `subagent-spawn.*` family, `agent-consult-runtime`, `server.sessions.create`, `agent-runner-session-reset`, accessor suites, plus the command/channel isolation suites the earlier CI run flagged (`agents.delete`, `channels.list`, `channel-setup/*`, `session.test.ts`)

target.title: fix(cron): default deleteAfterRun for isolated cron jobs
target.body:
## Summary
- Isolated cron sessions are intended as per-run scratch sessions, but periodic isolated jobs did not default to `deleteAfterRun=true`.
- Only one-shot (`schedule.kind === "at"`) jobs got the cleanup default, so recurring isolated runs left sessions alive and could keep consuming tokens after the run was marked ok.
- `normalizeCronJobCreate` now defaults `deleteAfterRun` to `true` whenever the resolved `sessionTarget` is `isolated`, while still preserving explicit `deleteAfterRun: false`.

Fixes #95907

## Real behavior proof
- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Periodic isolated cron jobs persisted their agent session after a run, allowing the session loop to keep consuming tokens.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux, Node 22.22.0, local source checkout.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  ```bash
  node --import tsx -e "
    import { normalizeCronJobCreate } from './src/cron/normalize.ts';
    const job = normalizeCronJobCreate({
      name: 'recurring isolated',
      enabled: true,
      schedule: { kind: 'cron', expr: '* * * * *' },
      sessionTarget: 'isolated',
      wakeMode: 'now',
      payload: { kind: 'agentTurn', message: 'hi' }
    });
    console.log(JSON.stringify(job, null, 2));
  "
  ```
- **Evidence after fix:**
  ```json
  {
    "name": "recurring isolated",
    "enabled": true,
    "schedule": { "kind": "cron", "expr": "* * * * *" },
    "sessionTarget": "isolated",
    "wakeMode": "now",
    "payload": { "kind": "agentTurn", "message": "hi" },
    "deleteAfterRun": true,
    "delivery": { "mode": "announce" }
  }
  ```
- **Observed result after fix:** A newly created recurring isolated cron job now has `deleteAfterRun: true` without an explicit user override.
- **What was not tested:** Live token accounting against a real model provider; the change is in normalization defaults and is covered by unit tests.

## Regression Test Plan
- Coverage level: Unit test
- Target test file: `src/cron/normalize.test.ts`
- Scenario locked in: `defaults deleteAfterRun for recurring isolated agent jobs`, `defaults deleteAfterRun for recurring isolated jobs from payload kind`, `preserves explicit deleteAfterRun=false for isolated jobs`, and `does not default deleteAfterRun for recurring main jobs`.
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: The fix lives entirely in normalization defaults, so asserting the normalized job shape covers the behavior and prevents regressions for both isolated and main targets.

## Root Cause
- Root cause: `normalizeCronJobInput` only defaulted `deleteAfterRun` for one-shot `schedule.kind === "at"` schedules. Recurring isolated jobs therefore fell through with `deleteAfterRun` undefined, so `cleanupCronRunSessionAfterRun` skipped session deletion and the isolated agent session stayed alive after the run.
- Missing detection / guardrail: No test asserted the default for recurring isolated jobs, and the default logic did not consider the `sessionTarget` ownership of the session.

target.title: fix(control-ui): show unavailable sizes for negative byte counts
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a narrow Control UI display bug where an invalid negative byte metric could still be formatted as if it were a real byte size.

The affected helper is `formatBytes()` in `ui/src/lib/agents/display.ts`. It already treats missing values and non-finite numbers as unavailable, but finite negative values previously passed through to the shared `formatByteSize()` formatter. Since byte counts represent cardinal quantities, a value like `-1` is not a meaningful UI size and should use the same unavailable marker as other invalid inputs.

In practice, this means Control UI status details could show a misleading negative size label instead of the existing `-` fallback when upstream/runtime data provides a malformed or sentinel-like negative byte count.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix keeps the behavior at the Control UI display boundary. The shared `formatByteSize()` helper remains a generic formatter for caller-provided numbers; this PR only tightens the wrapper that decides whether a byte metric is displayable in the UI.

Core production diff:

```diff
 export function formatBytes(bytes?: number) {
-  if (bytes == null || !Number.isFinite(bytes)) {
+  if (bytes == null || !Number.isFinite(bytes) || bytes < 0) {
     return "-";
   }
```

This intentionally preserves the existing formatting contract for valid values:

```text
undefined -> -
-1        -> -
0         -> 0 B
512       -> 512 B
1536      -> 1.5 KB
```

The colocated regression test adds the missing negative-input assertion while keeping the existing positive formatting assertions unchanged.

## User Impact

Users now see the unavailable marker `-` when Control UI receives an invalid negative byte count, rather than a negative byte-size label that looks like a valid measurement.

The visible effect is intentionally small and defensive: normal zero and positive byte displays continue to render exactly as before, while malformed negative metrics are no longer presented as meaningful sizes.

## Evidence

### Real Behavior Proof

This PR includes after-fix terminal proof from the current branch source, not only a unit-test claim. The temporary local script reads `ui/src/lib/agents/display.ts`, evaluates the exported `formatBytes()` function body from this PR, and imports the real shared formatter from `packages/normalization-core/src/format.ts`.

Observed output:

```text
Control UI byte formatter after-fix proof (current branch source)
formatBytes source: ui/src/lib/agents/display.ts
formatByteSize source: packages/normalization-core/src/format.ts
guard line: if (bytes == null || !Number.isFinite(bytes) || bytes < 0) {
formatBytes(-1): -
formatBytes(0): 0 B
formatBytes(512): 512 B
formatBytes(1536): 1.5 KB
```

This shows the changed runtime behavior directly: the invalid negative byte count now renders as the unavailable marker, while normal zero and positive byte formatting still renders unchanged.

GitHub validation also confirms the PR body contains acceptable real-behavior evidence:
- `Real behavior proof` passed on the current PR head

### Before/After Behavior Delta

This PR also includes direct before/after proof for the changed Control UI formatter boundary. The comparison uses `upstream/main` for the base behavior and the current PR head for the fixed behavior:

```text
Control UI byte formatter before/after proof
base source: upstream/main:ui/src/lib/agents/display.ts
head source: HEAD:ui/src/lib/agents/display.ts

base main:
formatBytes(-1): -1 B
formatBytes(0): 0 B
formatBytes(512): 512 B
formatBytes(1536): 1.5 KB

PR head:
formatBytes(-1): -
formatBytes(0): 0 B
formatBytes(512): 512 B
formatBytes(1536): 1.5 KB
```

This isolates the behavior changed by the PR: only the invalid negative byte count moves from a misleading byte-size label to the existing unavailable marker, while valid zero and positive byte counts keep the same display output.

### Regression Coverage

Focused regression coverage added:
- `formatBytes(-1)` returns `-`
- existing zero and positive byte formatting assertions remain unchanged

### Possible Call Chain / Impact

```text
Control UI status/detail data
  -> formatBytes(bytes)
  -> unavailable guard for nullish, non-finite, or negative values
  -> formatByteSize(...) only for valid zero/positive byte counts
  -> rendered byte-size label in Control UI
```

### Validation

- `git diff --check` passed
- GitHub `Real behavior proof` check passed on the current PR head
- `pnpm --dir ui test -- src/lib/agents/display.test.ts` was attempted locally, but the command ran the full UI suite and hit local environment failures unrelated to this diff: Chinese locale-formatted strings, missing Playwright Chromium, and a pre-existing Vite alias assertion. No production files outside `ui/src/lib/agents/display.ts` and `ui/src/lib/agents/display.test.ts` were changed.

AI-assisted: drafted and validated with Codex; I reviewed the change and understand the behavior.

target.title: fix(memory): exclude extraPaths from shared scope hash to avoid unnecessary reindexing
target.body:
## Problem

Changing `memorySearch.extraPaths` in agent config creates a new shared memory database (new SHA256 hash), requiring a full reindex. This is a regression from the shared-memory-by-directory design — extra paths are an index scope, not a store identity.

## Solution

`computeSharedScopeHash()` now only depends on `workspaceDir`. The engine already handles incremental indexing when new paths are added to the same store — no need to rehash on extraPaths changes.

New `packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/shared-store-registry.ts` added for tracking store-to-agent mappings.

## Changes

- **`src/agents/memory-search.ts`**: Remove `extraPaths` from hash; add `sharedStorePath` field; add `resolveAgentWorkspaceDir` import
- **`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/shared-store-registry.ts`**: New registry for shared store diagnostics
- **`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/engine-foundation.ts`**: Export `computeSharedScopeHash`
- **`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/engine-storage.ts`**: Export shared store registry helpers

## Upgrade Note

Existing shared databases named `shared-{old-hash}.sqlite` (which included extraPaths) will not match the new hash. Admins should rename the existing DB to the new hash or rebuild.

target.title: Hooks: chain global pre-commit guard
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw can use the repo-local `git-hooks/pre-commit` through `core.hooksPath=git-hooks`. In that setup, user-level machine-wide Git guards configured via global `core.hooksPath` do not run. That is a local defense gap for checks such as secret scanning and AI-context loss protection.

This PR makes the repo-local pre-commit hook chain the configured global `pre-commit` hook first when it exists and is executable, then continues with the existing OpenClaw staged-file lint/format flow.

Validation evidence:

- `bash -n git-hooks/pre-commit` passed.
- `git-hooks/pre-commit` passed with no staged files.
- `git diff --check origin/main..HEAD` passed.

- Problem: this repo can use `core.hooksPath=git-hooks`, which means the machine-wide Git pre-commit guard is bypassed.
- Why it matters: local security and AI-context guards should still run before project-specific formatting hooks.
- What changed: `git-hooks/pre-commit` now invokes the configured global `pre-commit` hook first when present, then continues with the existing staged-file lint/format flow.
